tools.name: audit_expense_portfolio
tools.title: Audit many expense statements at once
tools.description: Audit many landlord operating-expense (CAM) statements at once, for a tenant with many locations or for a lease audit firm or tenant-rep broker acting for one. Takes up to 50 audits, each the input audit_expense_statement takes (the lease's verified facts, the statement's verified facts, optionally the prior year's lines) plus a label and optionally the landlord, and one as_of date for all. Runs audit_expense_statement on each location (the same function, not a second implementation). Returns, per location, the audit's summary (findings by class, dollars at stake by class, the dispute deadline, the checks that could not run), its findings in short form with lease and statement pages, a reference to its full result (digests of its input and result; include_results returns the whole result) and its own package_items for fact_package_send; across the portfolio, totals by finding class and by check, dollars at stake in total and by landlord, the locations ranked by dollars at stake, dispute deadlines in date order with days remaining counted from as_of, repeated issues (the same check failing at several locations, or in several statement years for one landlord) and the locations whose input failed validation, each with its issues (the other locations are still audited). Deterministic and no model: same inputs, same answer, no clock. Findings are differences against quoted terms, not legal conclusions. On the hosted API the answer carries, for each location, its own attestation (the one audit_expense_statement returns for that location's input), so each location's package is sent to its own landlord and checked on its own through fact_package_send; a service without a signing key returns none and says so. On the hosted API, callers without a Pro or Team key get the summary only (counts and totals); the one free full document of an email-verified account covers a single audit (audit_expense_statement), not a portfolio, and the answer says so. Metering: the portfolio report (report_create kind expense_audit_portfolio) counts one unit of the monthly report allowance for each location audited in full (report_units); this tool call is not counted, as audit_expense_statement is not.

label.description: Required: the location's name as the person knows it (a store number, a property name, a suite), 1 to 120 characters, unique within the call. Printed in the answer and the report.

landlord.description: Optional: the landlord organisation named on the statement, as typed (at most 200 characters). Locations with the same landlord (compared by letters and digits only) are totalled together and checked for repeated issues. Left out: the location is totalled under 'Landlord not named'.

lease_facts.description: Required: the location's lease facts, exactly as audit_expense_statement's lease_facts (an array of verified facts, each with its quote and page).

statement_facts.description: Required: the landlord's statement as verified facts, exactly as audit_expense_statement's statement_facts.

prior_statement_facts.description: Optional: the prior year's statement.line and statement.period facts for this location, as audit_expense_statement's prior_statement_facts.

yoy_threshold.description: Optional: this location's year-over-year threshold, a number above 0 and at most 10, as audit_expense_statement's yoy_threshold. Default: the call's yoy_threshold.

audits.description: Up to 50 audits, one per location (or per location and year), each the input audit_expense_statement takes (lease_facts, statement_facts, prior_statement_facts, yoy_threshold) plus a label and optionally the landlord. An entry that fails validation is reported with its issues under locations_invalid and the others are audited; the call does not fail for it.

as_of.description: Today's date, YYYY-MM-DD, for every location. The tool reads no clock: every deadline's days remaining is counted from this date.

yoy_threshold.description: A line that rose by more than this fraction over the prior year is listed as a question to ask (default 0.10 = 10%), for every location that does not set its own. Must be greater than 0.

include_results.description: True: each location also carries its whole audit_expense_statement result (every finding with its quotes, pages and calculation steps) under result. Default false: each location carries its summary, its findings in short form and result_ref (the digests of its input and result, to check a result against).

tools.name: audit_expense_statement
tools.title: Audit a landlord's expense statement against the lease
tools.description: Audit a landlord's operating-expense (CAM) statement for a tenant, from verified facts only. Give the lease's facts (doc_abstract_lease or doc_verify_facts: pro-rata share, cap, base year or stop, admin fee, gross-up, excluded categories, capital-item treatment, audit right) and the statement's facts (each billed line, share applied, fee, gross-up, cap applied, totals, estimates, the date the tenant received it), each with its quote and page and passing fact_validate; optionally the prior year's lines. Returns findings, each with a stable code, the landlord's figure, the figure the lease yields, the dollar difference, the lease and statement fact ids with the quotes and pages, the calculation steps, a confidence class (follows_from_terms: the arithmetic follows from a quoted term and the statement's own numbers; depends_on_reading: it depends on how the lease sentence is read; question_to_ask: a question, never an overcharge) and what a person must confirm; totals; the last day to dispute or invoke the audit right with the notice form the lease requires; whether the difference crosses the lease's cost-shifting threshold; package_items ready for fact_package_send (state_ours with the landlord's figure as their_value for each finding, accept_theirs for lines with no finding); and checks_not_run with the reason (a missing lease term is never guessed). Twelve checks: management fee, cap, capital items, gross-up, pro-rata share, excluded categories, duplicates, base year or stop, arithmetic, year over year, deadlines, cost-shifting. Deterministic and no model: a finding without a verified lease fact behind it is never produced; same inputs, same findings; as_of is an input. Findings are differences against quoted terms, not legal conclusions: each finding carries its quote, for a person to review before anything is sent. On the hosted API the whole answer also carries attestation, the service's signature over the items, grades and figures that fact_package_send carries, so the FactLot record can show them as computed by FactLot and unchanged since; a service without a signing key returns none and says so. On the hosted API, callers without a Pro or Team key get the summary only (finding count, total difference, deadlines, checks not run) and the answer says what is withheld. Each free, email-verified account (an fl_free_ key) gets one whole document in total across audit_expense_statement, estoppel_prepare and rent_roll_certify: that answer says so, and the report built from the same arguments is included for 24 hours; Pro and Team include every document with the monthly allowance.

lease_facts.description: The lease's verified facts (doc_abstract_lease's facts, or doc_verify_facts' verified[].fact), each with its quote and page. Read by predicate: lease.pro_rata_share (number; required: every finding rests on it), lease.pro_rata_basis {tenant_sf, building_sf}, lease.cam_cap {method, rate} or, when the lease says only 'cumulative' or 'non-cumulative' and not how, lease.cam_cap_rate {rate} (the audit then shows the figure under each of the three methods), lease.operating_expense_base_year (integer), lease.expense_stop {amount} (building-level USD per year), lease.cam_admin_fee {rate, base: actual|grossed_up, excluded_from_base: [category words]}, lease.cam_gross_up {target_occupancy, applies_to: variable_expenses|all_expenses, base_year_grossed_up?: boolean}, lease.cam_exclusion (one per excluded category: a string, or {category, keywords?: [words]}), lease.capex_treatment {keywords: [words], recoverable: excluded|amortized, amortization_years?, interest_rate?}, lease.audit_right {window_days, starts_from: statement_receipt|statement_date, notice_form, auditor?, cost_shift_threshold?: {type: percent_of_billed|amount, value}}. A check whose lease term is missing is listed in checks_not_run; nothing is guessed.

statement_facts.description: The landlord's statement as verified facts, each with its quote and page. Read by predicate: statement.period {year, statement_date, received_date}, statement.line {label, amount (building-level USD), controllable?, variable?, capital?, grossed_up_amount?, amortization?: {cost, years, rate}} (one per billed line), statement.total {amount}, statement.share_applied {share, building_sf?}, statement.gross_up {actual_occupancy, target_occupancy}, statement.admin_fee {rate, base_amount, amount}, statement.cap_reference {year, amount} (the tenant's controllable amount in the cap's reference year), statement.cap_applied {limit: number or null}, statement.base_year_applied {base_year?, stop_amount?, deduction, grossed_up?}, statement.base_year_total {year, amount}, statement.separately_billed {label, amount}, statement.tenant_charge {amount}, statement.estimates_credited {amount}, statement.estimates_paid {amount}, statement.balance_claimed {amount}.

prior_statement_facts.description: Optional: the prior year's statement.line and statement.period facts, for the year-over-year questions.

as_of.description: Today's date, YYYY-MM-DD. The tool reads no clock: deadlines are counted from this date.

yoy_threshold.description: A line that rose by more than this fraction over the prior year is listed as a question to ask (default 0.10 = 10%). Never an overcharge. Must be greater than 0.

tools.name: calc_amortization_schedule
tools.title: Loan amortization schedule
tools.description: Period-by-period schedule of a fixed-rate loan, monthly or quarterly: an optional interest-only period, then level payments on an amortization term that can run past maturity (balloon), with 30/360, actual/360, or actual/365 interest (the payment on a 30/360 basis). Rows are in cents that foot: interest is rounded each period, the final payment repays the whole balance, and the totals are the row sums. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.amortization_schedule@1, every step, and any warnings.

principal.description: Loan amount funded, USD. Must be greater than 0.

rate_annual.description: Fixed nominal annual interest rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.065 for 6.5%. Must be less than 1.

payment_frequency.description: Payment period: monthly (12 a year) or quarterly (4 a year). Term, amortization, and interest-only months must be whole periods.

term_months.description: Months from funding to maturity, when any remaining balance (the balloon) is repaid.

amortization_months.description: Amortization period in months that sets the level payment after any interest-only period, e.g. 360 for a 30-year schedule; 0 means interest-only to maturity. Must be at least term_months − interest_only_months (a shorter schedule would repay the loan before maturity).

interest_only_months.description: Months of interest-only payments at the start of the loan; amortization over amortization_months begins after them. At most term_months.

day_count.description: Interest day count: "30/360" (each period is 30 days a month: interest = balance × rate ÷ periods a year), "actual/360" or "actual/365" (balance × rate × actual days in the period ÷ 360 or 365; needs start_date). Under actual day counts the level payment is still computed on a 30/360 basis, as US commercial loans usually are, so the balloon absorbs the difference.

start_date.description: Funding date, YYYY-MM-DD. Payment k falls k periods later on the same day of the month (clamped to month end); the first period runs from this date to the first payment date. Required for actual/360 and actual/365; optional for 30/360, where it only dates the rows.

tools.name: calc_cam_reconciliation
tools.title: CAM / operating expense reconciliation
tools.description: Reconcile a tenant's annual CAM charge: exclusions, occupancy gross-up of variable expenses, pro rata share, controllable-expense caps (compounding_from_base, simple_from_base, year_over_year), an admin fee (before or after the cap, inside or outside it, with per-line exclusions), base year or expense stop, partial-year occupancy (move-in/move-out prorates share, cap, and base by days), and estimates paid. Returns balance due and a full trace with order-of-operations warnings. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.cam_reconciliation@2, every step, and any warnings.

year.description: Calendar or lease year being reconciled.

pro_rata_share.description: Tenant's pro rata share, 0 < share ≤ 1 (e.g. 12,000 / 150,000 = 0.08). Must be greater than 0.

category.description: Expense line as named in the operating statement, e.g. "janitorial".

amount.description: Building-level actual expense for the year, USD.

controllable.description: Subject to the cap. Taxes, insurance, and utilities are typically uncontrollable. Default true; under a cap, lines left unset are named in warnings.

recoverable.description: Excluded expenses (capital items, landlord-only costs) are dropped entirely.

variable.description: Varies with occupancy, so eligible for gross-up (janitorial, utilities, management fee). Default false; with a gross-up, lines left unset are named in warnings.

admin_fee_applies.description: Included in the admin_fee base. Set false for lines the lease excludes from the fee (often taxes, insurance, utilities, or a management fee already charged).

expenses.description: Building operating expense lines for the year.

gross_up.description: Gross up variable expenses to the target occupancy when actual occupancy is lower. Omit if the lease has no gross-up.

actual_occupancy.description: Average occupancy for the year, e.g. 0.82. Must be greater than 0.

target_occupancy.description: Gross-up occupancy stated in the lease (commonly 0.95 or 1.0). Must be greater than 0.

structure.description: Expense structure from the lease. Default: net.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its full share of recoverable expenses (NNN / net).

base_year_expenses.description: Total building recoverable expenses in the base year, already grossed up, USD.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over base-year expenses.

stop_amount.description: Building-level expense stop, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over a fixed expense stop.

cap.description: Cap on the tenant's share of controllable expenses. Omit if the lease has no cap.

method.description: compounding_from_base: reference × (1+rate)^years (often called cumulative, compounding). simple_from_base: reference × (1 + rate × years) (cumulative, non-compounding). year_over_year: prior year's capped amount × (1+rate) (non-cumulative). Map the lease language to one of these explicitly.

rate.description: Annual cap as a decimal, e.g. 0.05. Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

reference_amount.description: Tenant's share of controllable expenses in the reference year: the base year for *_from_base, or the prior year's capped amount for year_over_year, USD.

years_elapsed.description: Years since the base year (required for `*_from_base`).

admin_fee.description: Administrative fee the lease adds to the tenant's share. Omit if the lease has none.

rate.description: Administrative or management fee as a decimal of the fee base, e.g. 0.15 for 15%. The base is the tenant's share of recoverable lines with admin_fee_applies (after gross-up). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

applied.description: Fee on controllable lines computed on the tenant's share before the cap (before_cap) or on the capped amount (after_cap). Fees on uncontrollable lines are never capped. Irrelevant without a cap.

capped.description: True when the fee on controllable lines counts toward the controllable cap (controllable share plus fee may not exceed the cap limit); false adds it outside the cap.

occupancy.description: Partial-year occupancy: the tenant's share, cap limit, and base-year or stop deduction are prorated by occupied days ÷ period days (both inclusive), so a full-year cap and base are not applied to a part year. Omit for a full year.

move_in_date.description: Date the tenant's share starts within the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_start_date.

move_out_date.description: Last day of the tenant's share within the period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_end_date.

period_start_date.description: First day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to January 1 of year; set it for a lease year.

period_end_date.description: Last day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days after the start). Defaults to December 31 of year.

estimates_paid.description: Estimated CAM payments the tenant made during the year, USD (total for the year, not monthly).

tools.name: calc_capex_recovery
tools.title: Capital expenditure recovery
tools.description: Recoverable capital expenditure under a lease clause: amortize a capital cost over its useful life or the lease-specified period, straight-line (declining interest) or level payment, with interest on the unamortized balance or none; optionally cap each year's recovery at demonstrated cost savings (with or without carry-forward); and allocate each year to tenants by pro rata share. Every assumption is echoed with an optional lease clause citation. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.capex_recovery@1, every step, and any warnings.

cost.description: Capital cost of the improvement to recover, USD (building level). Must be greater than 0.

amortization_years.description: Years over which the cost is recovered: the useful life, or the amortization period the lease specifies.

period_basis.description: Where amortization_years comes from: useful_life (e.g. under GAAP or tax guidance) or lease_specified (a period the lease states). Labels only.

method.description: straight_line: equal principal (cost ÷ years) plus interest on the declining unamortized balance, so recovery falls each year. level_payment: a level annual payment like a mortgage, cost × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−years), split into interest and principal. Identical when interest_rate_annual is 0.

interest_rate_annual.description: Annual interest on the unamortized balance as a decimal, e.g. 0.08; 0 (default) for none. Charged on the balance at the start of each year. Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

first_year.description: Calendar or lease year of the first recovery year, e.g. 2026; labels the schedule rows. Omit to number years 1, 2, 3.

cost_savings_cap.description: Cost-savings limit: recovery in each year may not exceed the operating-cost savings the improvement demonstrably produces. Omit if the lease has none.

annual_savings.description: Demonstrated operating-cost savings per year, USD, the same every year. Give this or savings_by_year.

savings_by_year.description: Demonstrated savings for each recovery year, USD, one per year of amortization_years. Give this or annual_savings.

carry_forward.description: True if amortization disallowed by the cap in one year may be recovered in a later year of the period (still within that year's savings); false (default) if it is lost.

tenants.description: Tenants to allocate the annual recoverable amount to by pro rata share. Shares may sum to less than 1 (the landlord bears the rest), not more. Omit for the building-level schedule only.

pro_rata_share.description: Tenant's pro rata share of the recoverable amount, 0 < share ≤ 1. Must be greater than 0.

clauses.description: Lease clause behind each assumption, free text, echoed in the result's assumptions so a reviewer can check each against the lease.

cost.description: Free-text lease reference for this assumption, e.g. "Lease §6.2(b)" or "First Amendment ¶4". Echoed with the assumption.

amortization_period.description: Free-text lease reference for this assumption, e.g. "Lease §6.2(b)" or "First Amendment ¶4". Echoed with the assumption.

interest.description: Free-text lease reference for this assumption, e.g. "Lease §6.2(b)" or "First Amendment ¶4". Echoed with the assumption.

method.description: Free-text lease reference for this assumption, e.g. "Lease §6.2(b)" or "First Amendment ¶4". Echoed with the assumption.

cost_savings_cap.description: Free-text lease reference for this assumption, e.g. "Lease §6.2(b)" or "First Amendment ¶4". Echoed with the assumption.

pro_rata_share.description: Free-text lease reference for this assumption, e.g. "Lease §6.2(b)" or "First Amendment ¶4". Echoed with the assumption.

tools.name: calc_compare_proposals
tools.title: Compare lease proposals
tools.description: Rank 2–20 lease proposals with different terms, sizes, free rent, TI, concessions, and operating-expense structures (gross, NNN, base year, expense stop, with opex growth) on one discounted $/SF/yr basis, per rentable or usable SF (load factor): effective occupancy cost (tenant perspective) or discounted net effective rent after landlord-borne opex and optional pre-commencement downtime (landlord perspective). Cash flows monthly in advance at annual rate ÷ 12; warns when the usable-SF ranking differs and when terms differ. schedule.unit (kw, mw, unit, acre, key, room, space, the same for every proposal) ranks per kW, MW, unit, acre, key, room, or space instead of per SF. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.compare_proposals@2, every step, and any warnings.

perspective.description: Whose economics to rank on: tenant (effective occupancy cost, lower is better) or landlord (discounted net effective rent, higher is better).

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to every proposal (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12, cash flows at the start of each month). Default 0.08, named in warnings when omitted: the ranking can change with the rate. Must be less than 1.

area_basis.description: Area the $/SF/yr metric is divided by: rentable (schedule.area_sf, the default) or usable (each proposal's usable_sf, or area_sf ÷ load_factor). Rents and expenses stay quoted per rentable SF; use usable when proposals have different load factors and the tenant needs a fixed usable area.

name.description: Unique label for the proposal, e.g. building name.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

area_sf.description: Rentable square feet, or the quantity leased in unit (kW, MW, units, acres, keys, rooms, spaces) when unit is set. Must be greater than 0.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5; per unit per year when unit is set (a $/kW/month quote × 12).

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound. Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year (or per unit per year when unit is set) added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

unit.description: What area_sf and the per-SF fields measure: sf (default, square feet), kw or mw (data-center critical load), unit (apartment or other unit), acre (ground or yard lease), key or room (hotel), or space (parking). Every number is computed exactly as for square feet; the unit changes labels, steps, and warnings and adds unit and rate_unit to the result. Fields keep their _sf and _psf names: with unit kw, area_sf holds kW and starting_rent_psf_annual holds $/kW/yr. Omit for square feet.

schedule.description: Base-rent terms of this proposal (same input as calc_rent_schedule); schedule.area_sf is the rentable area. With schedule.unit (kw, mw, unit, acre, key, room, space), area_sf and every $/SF field of this proposal are per that unit; all proposals must use the same unit.

usable_sf.description: Usable square feet of this proposal (at most schedule.area_sf). Give this or load_factor, not both; required for area_basis usable. Must be greater than 0.

load_factor.description: Rentable ÷ usable area, e.g. 1.15 (usable_sf = area_sf ÷ load_factor). Give this or usable_sf, not both.

ti_allowance_psf.description: TI allowance paid by the landlord, USD per rentable SF, once at commencement (not per year).

other_concessions.description: Other cash concessions to the tenant at commencement (moving allowance, buyout), USD.

leasing_commissions.description: Leasing commissions paid by landlord at commencement, USD (landlord perspective only).

operating_expenses.description: Operating-expense structure of this proposal: gross, nnn, base_year, or expense_stop, with a lease-year-1 estimate and growth. Tenant perspective adds what the tenant pays; landlord perspective deducts what the landlord bears. Omit to price no operating expenses (as before).

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses the landlord pays, $/SF/yr in lease year 1 (used in the landlord perspective; the tenant pays none).

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

oneOf.description: Full-service gross: the landlord pays all operating expenses; the tenant pays none beyond base rent.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

oneOf.description: Net (NNN): the tenant pays all operating expenses, estimated at expense_psf_annual in lease year 1.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

stop_psf_annual.description: Expense stop, $/SF/yr: the tenant pays operating expenses above this fixed amount.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

tenant_upfront_costs.description: Tenant's own costs at commencement not covered by allowances (TI overage, moving), USD.
