tools.name: calc_critical_dates
tools.title: Lease critical dates
tools.description: Dated list of a lease's notice deadlines and option windows, from its expiration date and options: each renewal option's notice deadline or notice window and renewal term (successive options count back from the term before), each termination option's last day to give notice, an expansion option deadline, and other deadlines (a stated date, or N days after a date such as a ROFO notice). Calendar months; N months before a date keeps the day of month, clamped to a shorter month's end (a warning gives the month-end reading when it is later). Deadlines on a weekend or US federal holiday (5 U.S.C. §6103, observed days included) are flagged, or rolled to the preceding or following business day when business_day_roll says so. With as_of: days to each event, passed deadlines warned, and the next deadline. Steps show each computation. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.critical_dates@1, every step, and any warnings.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date of the current term (YYYY-MM-DD), as the lease or the latest amendment states it.

commencement_date.description: Commencement date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; listed as an event and checked to be before expiration_date.

as_of.description: Date to measure from (YYYY-MM-DD), usually today. Deadlines before it are flagged as passed; next_deadline is the first one on or after it.

renewal_option.description: Renewal options, as lease.renewal_option states them: each is exercised by notice counted back from the expiration in effect when it is exercised.

term_months.description: Length of each renewal term in calendar months.

notice_months.description: Notice "no later than N months before" the date it counts back from, in calendar months.

notice_days.description: Notice "no later than N days before" the date it counts back from, in calendar days.

notice_window.description: A notice window ("not earlier than 18 nor later than 12 months before expiration"), instead of notice_months or notice_days.

earliest_months_before.description: The window opens this many calendar months before the expiration in effect (notice given earlier is premature).

latest_months_before.description: The window closes this many calendar months before the expiration in effect (the last day to give notice).

termination_options.description: Early termination options, as lease.termination_option states them; notice counts back from each effective_date.

effective_date.description: Date the early termination takes effect (YYYY-MM-DD).

notice_months.description: Notice "no later than N months before" the date it counts back from, in calendar months.

notice_days.description: Notice "no later than N days before" the date it counts back from, in calendar days.

label.description: Name for this option, e.g. "Year 5 termination right".

expansion_option_deadline.description: Last day to exercise an expansion option (lease.expansion_option_deadline), YYYY-MM-DD.

other_deadlines.description: Other deadlines: expansion rights, ROFO or ROFR response periods, contraction rights.

label.description: What the deadline is, e.g. "ROFO response for Suite 410".

date.description: The deadline, when the lease states the date.

from_date.description: Or the date it counts from (e.g. the day Landlord's ROFO notice was received), with days_after.

business_day_roll.description: What to do with a deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday: "none" (default) keeps the date and flags it; "preceding" moves it to the business day before (never later than the lease date: the safe choice); "following" moves it to the next business day, which only a lease clause that says so allows.

holidays.description: Holidays that are not business days: "us_federal" (the eleven US federal holidays of 5 U.S.C. §6103(a), with the federal observed day when one falls on a weekend) or "none" (weekends only).

tools.name: calc_dcf_pro_forma
tools.title: Property DCF from a rent roll
tools.description: Property-level discounted cash flow from an in-place rent roll: each lease's rent, escalations, remaining term, and expense recovery (NNN, gross, base year), then at expiration one blended lease weighted by the renewal probability (renewal vs new-tenant rent, free rent, TI, leasing commissions, and new-tenant downtime, with fractional downtime and free rent kept as part months rather than rounded); market rent growth, general vacancy and credit loss, operating expenses, management fee, and capital reserves. Returns the annual cash-flow table (NOI and cash flow before debt) for the hold plus one year, the exit value at a cap rate on forward (or trailing) NOI less selling costs, the value (PV at the discount rate, end-of-year or mid-year), and with a purchase price the NPV, unlevered IRR, and equity multiple, with every lease event and convention stated. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.dcf_pro_forma@2, every step, and any warnings.

hold_years.description: Holding period in years. The property is sold at the end of the last year; one more year is projected for the forward NOI.

area_sf.description: Leased area, SF. Must be greater than 0.

rent_psf_annual.description: Current in-place base rent, USD/SF/yr (0 for space vacant at the start).

months_remaining.description: Months left on the lease from the analysis start: the lease runs through this month (1 = expires at the end of month 1). 0 means the space is vacant at the start and is leased to a new tenant after downtime_months.

escalation_rate.description: Annual bump in the in-place rent, e.g. 0.03, applied first in next_escalation_month and every 12 months after. Must be less than 1.

next_escalation_month.description: Analysis month of the next in-place rent bump (default 13, the start of year 2). Use the lease's anniversary month.

free_rent_months_remaining.description: Months of in-place free base rent still to run from the analysis start (months 1 to this are abated).

base_year_opex_psf_annual.description: Operating expenses in the lease's base year, USD/SF/yr: the tenant pays the excess above it. Required when recovery is base_year.

market_rent_psf_annual.description: Market rent for this space today, USD/SF/yr. Grows at market_rent_growth_rate each analysis year.

renewal_probability.description: Probability the tenant renews at expiration, 0 to 1 (e.g. 0.65). Blends the renewal and new-tenant assumptions below.

lease_term_months.description: Term of each lease signed at rollover (renewal or new tenant), months.

downtime_months.description: Months vacant before a new tenant starts paying (no downtime is assumed on renewal). Blended downtime = (1 − renewal_probability) × this, kept fractional, not rounded: the suite is vacant for the whole months and the rollover lease's first month collects 1 − the fraction of its rent and recoveries (0.45 months of downtime: the first month collects 55%).

renewal_rent_pct_of_market.description: Renewal rent as a share of market rent, e.g. 0.95 for a 5% renewal discount; new tenants pay market rent. Must be greater than 0.

rent_escalation_rate.description: Annual bump in a rollover lease's base rent, compounding every 12 months from its start, e.g. 0.03. Must be less than 1.

free_rent_months_new.description: Months of free base rent for a new tenant at the start of its lease.

free_rent_months_renewal.description: Months of free base rent on a renewal. Blended free rent = p × this + (1 − p) × free_rent_months_new, kept fractional: the whole months are fully abated and the next month by the fraction.

ti_psf_new.description: Tenant improvement allowance for a new tenant, USD/SF in today's dollars (grown at market_rent_growth_rate to the lease start).

ti_psf_renewal.description: Tenant improvement allowance on a renewal, USD/SF in today's dollars.

lc_rate_new.description: Leasing commission for a new tenant as a share of the base rent payable over the lease term after free rent, e.g. 0.06. Must be less than 1.

lc_rate_renewal.description: Leasing commission on a renewal, same basis, e.g. 0.03. Must be less than 1.

recovery.description: Expense recovery on rollover leases: "nnn" (tenant pays its share of operating expenses), "gross" (none), or "base_year" (expenses above the lease's first-year level).

leasing.description: Per-lease overrides of market_leasing (any subset of its fields).

leases.description: Rent roll: one entry per lease or vacant suite (at most 200). The building area is the sum of their areas.

renewal_probability.description: Probability the tenant renews at expiration, 0 to 1 (e.g. 0.65). Blends the renewal and new-tenant assumptions below.

lease_term_months.description: Term of each lease signed at rollover (renewal or new tenant), months.

downtime_months.description: Months vacant before a new tenant starts paying (no downtime is assumed on renewal). Blended downtime = (1 − renewal_probability) × this, kept fractional, not rounded: the suite is vacant for the whole months and the rollover lease's first month collects 1 − the fraction of its rent and recoveries (0.45 months of downtime: the first month collects 55%).

renewal_rent_pct_of_market.description: Renewal rent as a share of market rent, e.g. 0.95 for a 5% renewal discount; new tenants pay market rent. Must be greater than 0.

rent_escalation_rate.description: Annual bump in a rollover lease's base rent, compounding every 12 months from its start, e.g. 0.03. Must be less than 1.

free_rent_months_new.description: Months of free base rent for a new tenant at the start of its lease.

free_rent_months_renewal.description: Months of free base rent on a renewal. Blended free rent = p × this + (1 − p) × free_rent_months_new, kept fractional: the whole months are fully abated and the next month by the fraction.

ti_psf_new.description: Tenant improvement allowance for a new tenant, USD/SF in today's dollars (grown at market_rent_growth_rate to the lease start).

ti_psf_renewal.description: Tenant improvement allowance on a renewal, USD/SF in today's dollars.

lc_rate_new.description: Leasing commission for a new tenant as a share of the base rent payable over the lease term after free rent, e.g. 0.06. Must be less than 1.

lc_rate_renewal.description: Leasing commission on a renewal, same basis, e.g. 0.03. Must be less than 1.

recovery.description: Expense recovery on rollover leases: "nnn" (tenant pays its share of operating expenses), "gross" (none), or "base_year" (expenses above the lease's first-year level).

market_leasing.description: Market leasing assumptions applied at every lease expiration (and to space vacant at the start). A lease's own `leasing` object overrides any of them.

market_rent_growth_rate.description: Annual market rent growth, e.g. 0.03. Market rent and TI in analysis year y = today's × (1 + g)^(y − 1). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 1.

operating_expenses_psf_annual.description: Year-1 recoverable operating expenses, USD/SF/yr over the whole building area.

non_recoverable_expenses_annual.description: Year-1 operating expenses no tenant reimburses, USD/yr.

expense_growth_rate.description: Annual growth of operating expenses and capital reserves, e.g. 0.03: year y = year 1 × (1 + g)^(y − 1). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 1.

management_fee_rate.description: Management fee as a share of effective gross revenue, e.g. 0.03; not recovered. Must be less than 1.

general_vacancy_rate.description: General vacancy allowance as a share of gross revenue (base rent after free rent, plus recoveries), on top of the downtime modelled at rollover. Must be less than 1.

credit_loss_rate.description: Credit loss as a share of gross revenue, on top of general vacancy. Must be less than 1.

capital_reserve_psf_annual.description: Year-1 capital reserve, USD/SF/yr over the building area, below NOI. Grows with expense_growth_rate.

exit_cap_rate.description: Exit (terminal) cap rate applied to the exit NOI, e.g. 0.07. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

exit_noi_basis.description: "forward": the NOI of the year after the hold (the usual convention); "trailing": the NOI of the final hold year.

selling_cost_rate.description: Selling costs as a share of the gross sale price, e.g. 0.02. Must be less than 1.

discount_rate.description: Annual unlevered discount rate, e.g. 0.08. The present value at this rate is the value. Must be less than 1.

timing.description: "end_of_year": each year's cash flow is discounted (1 + r)^y (Excel NPV). "mid_year": operating cash flows at (1 + r)^(y − 0.5); the sale is always discounted at the end of the hold.

purchase_price.description: Price paid at the start, USD. Adds the NPV (value − price), the unlevered IRR and the going-in cap rate on price. Must be greater than 0.

tools.name: calc_debt_sizing
tools.title: Loan sizing (LTV / DSCR / debt yield)
tools.description: Size the maximum loan under any combination of max LTV, min DSCR, and min debt yield for a given NOI, rate, and amortization. Reports the binding constraint, debt service, and resulting metrics; optionally a stress table over NOI, rate, and value shocks (max loan, binding constraint, LTV, DSCR, debt yield per scenario) and the refinance shortfall against an existing loan balance. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.debt_sizing@3, every step, and any warnings.

noi.description: Underwritten net operating income, USD/yr. Must be greater than 0.

value.description: Appraised or underwritten value, USD. Required when max_ltv is set. Must be greater than 0.

rate_annual.description: Annual interest rate, e.g. 0.065. Must be less than 1.

max_ltv.description: Maximum loan-to-value, e.g. 0.65. Must be greater than 0.

min_dscr.description: Minimum debt service coverage ratio, e.g. 1.25. Must be greater than 0.

min_debt_yield.description: Minimum debt yield (NOI ÷ loan), e.g. 0.09. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

round_down_to.description: Round the final loan amount down to this increment (lenders often use 1,000 or 10,000). Must be greater than 0.

existing_loan_balance.description: Balance of the loan being refinanced, USD. Adds a refinance result (shortfall or excess proceeds against the max loan) and a shortfall per stress scenario. Must be greater than 0.

stress.description: Stress table: every combination of the NOI, rate, and value shocks (up to 1,000 scenarios), each sized under the same constraints and rounding. The base result is unchanged.

noi_shocks.description: Relative NOI changes as decimals, e.g. [-0.05, -0.1, -0.2] for NOI down 5%, 10%, 20%. Omit for no NOI shock.

items.description: Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

rate_shocks.description: Absolute changes to rate_annual as decimals, e.g. [0.005, 0.01] for +50 and +100 bp. The stressed rate must stay at or above 0 and below 1. Omit for no rate shock.

items.description: Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 1.

value_shocks.description: Relative value changes as decimals, e.g. [-0.1, -0.2]; requires value. Omit for no value shock.

items.description: Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

value_moves_with_noi.description: Also scale value by each NOI shock (value × (1 + noi_shock), a constant cap rate), as a lender repricing value on stressed NOI would.

tools.name: calc_direct_cap
tools.title: Direct capitalization value and implied cap rate
tools.description: Value by direct capitalization: (NOI − capital reserve) ÷ cap rate, then below-the-line deductions for lease-up costs, free-rent burn-off, and other adjustments to an as-is value (optionally rounded); and the cap rate a price implies, before and after reserves and all-in after the below-the-line costs. Records the NOI basis (trailing, forward, stabilized). Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.direct_cap@1, every step, and any warnings.

noi.description: Net operating income to capitalize, USD/yr, before capital reserves (they are deducted separately below). Must be greater than 0.

noi_basis.description: What the NOI is: trailing 12 months (T-12), forward 12 months (year 1 of a pro forma), or stabilized. The cap rate must be on the same basis; this is recorded in the steps, not checked.

cap_rate.description: Capitalization rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.065 for 6.5%. Gives the value. Provide cap_rate, price, or both. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

price.description: Purchase or asking price, USD. Gives the implied cap rate. Provide cap_rate, price, or both. Must be greater than 0.

capex_reserve_annual.description: Annual capital (replacement) reserve deducted from NOI before capitalizing, USD/yr. 0 if the NOI is already after reserves.

lease_up_costs.description: One-time costs to reach the stabilized NOI (TI, leasing commissions, lost rent during lease-up), USD, deducted from the capitalized value.

free_rent_burn_off.description: Free rent still to be given under signed leases (rent the stabilized NOI assumes but the owner will not collect), USD, deducted from the capitalized value.

other_adjustments.description: Further below-the-line value adjustments, applied after capitalizing.

label.description: What the adjustment is, e.g. "deferred maintenance" or "excess land".

amount.description: USD added to the value: negative for a deduction (deferred maintenance), positive for an addition (excess land).

area_sf.description: Rentable area in SF, for value per SF. Optional. Must be greater than 0.

round_value_to.description: Also report the as-is value rounded to this increment (half away from zero), e.g. 100000 as appraisers round. Optional. Must be greater than 0.

tools.name: calc_equity_waterfall
tools.title: LP/GP equity distribution waterfall
tools.description: Split periodic project equity cash flows between LP and GP: preferred return (compounding or simple) and return of capital pro rata to capital in either order, an optional GP catch-up, IRR-hurdle tiers with promote splits measured on the LP's IRR, and a residual split. Returns per-period LP and GP contributions and distributions (with the GP's promote) that foot to the cent, and LP, GP, and project IRRs and multiples, with the conventions to confirm against the operating agreement. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.equity_waterfall@1, every step, and any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Project-level equity cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, … periods: negative = capital contributed by the investors, positive = cash available to distribute. At most 600.

periods_per_year.description: Cash-flow periods per year: 1 annual, 4 quarterly, 12 monthly. Sets the pref accrual per period and annualizes the IRRs.

lp_share.description: Share of every contribution funded by the LP, e.g. 0.9; the GP co-invests the rest (1 for no GP capital). Capital, pref, and the non-promote part of every split are shared in this ratio. Must be greater than 0.

pref.description: Preferred return on unreturned capital, paid to all investors pro rata to capital. Omit for none.

rate_annual.description: Preferred return, annual, e.g. 0.08. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

compounding.description: "compound": unpaid pref earns pref, at the effective periodic rate (1 + rate)^(1 ÷ periods_per_year) − 1, so a fully paid pref is an IRR of rate on the capital. "simple": each period accrues unreturned capital × rate ÷ periods_per_year, and unpaid pref earns nothing.

distribution_order.description: Which comes first from each distribution: accrued pref, then return of capital (the usual order), or capital first.

catch_up.description: GP catch-up after the pref and return of capital. Omit for none.

gp_share.description: Share of each catch-up dollar paid to the GP as promote, e.g. 1 for a full catch-up or 0.5 for a 50% catch-up; the rest goes to the investors pro rata. Must be greater than 0.

target_promote.description: Catch-up continues until the GP's promote is this share of all profit distributed so far (everything other than return of capital), e.g. 0.2. Must be below gp_share. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

tiers.description: IRR-hurdle tiers after the catch-up, in increasing until_irr order: each distributes with its promote until the LP's IRR reaches until_irr.

until_irr.description: LP IRR hurdle (annual, as calc_irr annualizes) that ends this tier, e.g. 0.12. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 10.

promote.description: Share of each dollar in this tier paid to the GP as promote, e.g. 0.2 for an 80/20 split; the rest goes to the investors pro rata to capital. Must be less than 1.

residual_promote.description: GP promote share of everything after the last tier, e.g. 0.3 for a 70/30 split. Must be less than 1.

tools.name: calc_exchange_1031
tools.title: 1031 exchange deadlines, identification, and boot
tools.description: Not tax advice: arithmetic only. The 45-day identification and 180-day exchange deadlines of IRC §1031(a)(3) (the exchange period ends earlier at a given tax-return due date), the three-property, 200%, and 95% identification tests of Treas. Reg. §1.1031(k)-1(c)(4), and the cash boot, mortgage boot, debt replacement, and trade-down of an exchange, with the boot-limited gain when the basis is given. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.exchange_1031@2, every step, and any warnings.

relinquished_transfer_date.description: Date the relinquished property was transferred (closed), YYYY-MM-DD. With several relinquished properties, the earliest transfer starts both periods.

tax_return_due_date.description: Due date, including extensions, of the taxpayer's federal return for the year of the transfer, YYYY-MM-DD. IRC §1031(a)(3)(B) ends the exchange period on this date if it is earlier than day 180. FactLot does not compute it.

as_of.description: Date to count the days remaining from, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

sale_price.description: Contract sale price (fair market value) of the relinquished property, USD. Also the base of the 200% identification test. Must be greater than 0.

selling_expenses.description: Exchange and closing expenses paid at the sale (commissions, title, QI fees), USD.

debt_relieved.description: Mortgages and other liabilities paid off or assumed by the buyer at the sale, USD.

adjusted_basis.description: Taxpayer's adjusted basis in the relinquished property, USD. Optional; adds the realized gain and the boot-limited gain.

cash_received_at_sale.description: Cash the taxpayer took from the sale proceeds instead of leaving them with the qualified intermediary, USD.

replacement.description: The property acquired (in total). Omit to check only the deadlines and identification.

purchase_price.description: Total price of the replacement property or properties acquired, USD.

acquisition_costs.description: Closing costs paid at the purchase, USD.

new_debt.description: New or assumed mortgage debt on the replacement property, USD.

identified_properties.description: Replacement properties identified in writing. Empty to skip the identification checks.

fair_market_value.description: Fair market value at the end of the identification period, USD. Must be greater than 0.

identified_date.description: Date the written identification was delivered, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; checked against the 45-day deadline.

received.description: Whether the taxpayer acquired this property.

received_date.description: Date it was acquired, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; checked against the exchange deadline.

tools.name: calc_hotel_metrics
tools.title: Hotel operating metrics (USALI)
tools.description: Occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, TRevPAR, and a USALI-style profit ladder for a period: departmental profit, GOP and margin, GOPPAR, management fees, EBITDA, FF&E reserve, and NOI (EBITDA less replacement reserve). Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.hotel_metrics@1, every step, and any warnings.

nights.description: Nights in the period, e.g. 365 for a year or 30 for a month.

rooms_out_of_order.description: Room-nights (rooms × nights, not rooms) taken off the market in the period, e.g. 20 rooms closed for a 30-night renovation = 600. Subtracted from rooms × nights to give rooms available. USALI (11th ed.) keeps short-term out-of-order rooms in rooms available; include only rooms formally removed from sale.

rooms_sold.description: Room-nights occupied by paying guests in the period (USALI: rooms sold, excluding complimentary rooms).

room_revenue.description: Rooms revenue for the period, USD (USALI Rooms department revenue, net of taxes and allowances).

fb_revenue.description: Food and beverage revenue, USD (USALI Food and Beverage department revenue).

other_revenue.description: Other operated departments plus miscellaneous income, USD (USALI Other Operated Departments and Miscellaneous Income).

departmental_expenses.description: Total departmental expenses, USD: rooms, F&B, and other operated departments (USALI Total Departmental Expenses).

undistributed_expenses.description: Total undistributed operating expenses, USD: administrative and general, information and telecommunications, sales and marketing, property operation and maintenance, utilities (USALI Total Undistributed Operating Expenses).

management_fee_rate.description: Base management fee as a share of total operating revenue, e.g. 0.03 (USALI Management Fees). Must be less than 1.

management_fee_fixed.description: Fixed or incentive management fee for the period, USD, added to the percentage fee (USALI Management Fees).

non_operating_expenses.description: Property taxes, insurance, ground rent, and other non-operating expenses, USD (USALI Non-Operating Income and Expenses).

ffe_reserve_rate.description: FF&E replacement reserve as a share of total operating revenue, e.g. 0.04 (USALI Replacement Reserve, below EBITDA). Must be less than 1.

tools.name: calc_irr
tools.title: Internal rate of return
tools.description: Periodic and annualized IRR of periodic cash flows, as decimals (0.085 = 8.5%), solved deterministically by scanning a 1-point grid of per-period rates and bisecting each sign change; reports every root it finds when cash flows have multiple IRRs (two roots within one grid step can be missed). Errors when the flows do not change sign or no root lies between -99.99% and 1000% per period. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.irr@2, every step, and any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Periodic cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, …; negative for outflows (e.g. purchase price at t = 0). At most 1200.

periods_per_year.description: Cash-flow periods per year, used only to annualize the result: 1 for annual flows, 4 for quarterly, 12 for monthly.

tools.name: calc_lease_remeasurement_asc842
tools.title: Lease remeasurement (ASC 842, lessee)
tools.description: Remeasure a lessee's lease liability and right-of-use asset under ASC 842 after a modification, lease-term reassessment, contingency resolution, or residual value guarantee change: new liability (PV of remaining payments), liability and ROU adjustments with any gain (ASC 842-20-35-4), and the per-period amortization table (operating: straight-line single lease cost; finance: interest plus amortization) in cents that foots: every row rolls forward exactly, totals are the row sums, and the final period trues up liability and ROU asset to zero. Warns where judgment is needed. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.lease_remeasurement_asc842@2, every step, and any warnings.

classification.description: Lessee classification (ASC 842-10-25-2): operating (single straight-line lease cost) or finance (interest on the liability plus straight-line ROU amortization).

period.description: Period index counted from the remeasurement date (1 = first remaining period).

amount.description: Lease payment due in that period after the event, USD for the period (a monthly amount when periods_per_year is 12, not annualized): fixed and in-substance fixed payments, less incentives receivable (ASC 842-10-30-5).

payments.description: Remaining lease payments after the event, in ascending period order. Periods not listed carry no payment (rent-free).

remaining_periods.description: Remaining lease term in periods after the event. Defaults to the last period index in payments; set it higher when the final periods are rent-free.

payment_timing.description: Whether each payment falls at the beginning (in advance) or end (in arrears) of its period.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate applied to the remaining payments, e.g. 0.06. Nominal: the periodic rate is this ÷ periods_per_year. Must be less than 1.

periods_per_year.description: Payment periods per year (12 for monthly, 4 for quarterly).

discount_rate_updated.description: True when discount_rate_annual was determined at the remeasurement date (ASC 842-10-35-5: required for modifications and lease-term or purchase-option reassessments); false when it is the rate from commencement (kept for contingency resolutions and residual value guarantee changes).

liability_before.description: Carrying amount of the lease liability immediately before the remeasurement, USD.

rou_asset_before.description: Carrying amount of the right-of-use asset immediately before the remeasurement, USD (after any impairment).

event.description: What triggered the remeasurement: modification_extend_term / modification_shorten_term / modification_change_in_payments (a modification not accounted for as a separate contract, ASC 842-10-25-8 and 25-11), reassessment_of_term_or_option (ASC 842-10-35-1 and 35-4(c)), contingency_resolved (variable payments became fixed, ASC 842-10-35-4(b)), residual_value_guarantee_change (ASC 842-10-35-4(c)(3)), or index_or_rate_change (ASC 842-10-35-4: not a remeasurement trigger by itself; computed as if remeasured for another reason).

tools.name: calc_lease_vs_own
tools.title: Lease vs. own
tools.description: Compare leasing with buying over a fixed horizon: NPV of each case's annual cash costs (rent, free rent, tenant expenses, and move-in costs versus equity, debt service, owner expenses, reserves, and a sale at the horizon by stated value or exit cap rate), optionally after tax, with the year-by-year tables and the break-even residual value at which owning equals leasing. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.lease_vs_own@2, every step, and any warnings.

horizon_years.description: Analysis horizon in years. Both cases are compared over this period; the own case sells at the end of it.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to both cases' year-end cash flows (year 0 = closing / move-in). Must be less than 1.

annual_rent.description: Rent due in each year of the horizon, USD, year 1 first. Must have exactly horizon_years entries.

oneOf.description: Explicit rent per year.

escalation_rate_annual.description: Compounding annual bump, e.g. 0.03: rent_k = base × (1 + e)^(k − 1). Must be less than 1.

oneOf.description: Base rent with a compounding annual escalation.

rent.description: Annual rent, as an explicit schedule or base rent with escalation.

free_rent_months.description: Rent-free months at the start of the lease, abated from year 1 (and year 2 if more than 12). Must not exceed the horizon.

operating_expenses_annual.description: Year-1 operating expenses borne by the tenant on top of rent (NNN charges, utilities), USD per year.

expense_growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth applied to expenses after year 1, e.g. 0.03 (year k = year-1 amount × (1 + g)^(k − 1)). Must be less than 1.

upfront_costs.description: Tenant's one-time costs at move-in not covered by allowances: TI overage, moving, security deposit treated as cost, USD.

closing_costs.description: Acquisition closing costs, USD (added to the purchase price for cash and for depreciable basis).

loan.description: Acquisition financing. Omit for an all-cash purchase.

rate_annual.description: Annual interest rate, e.g. 0.065. Must be less than 1.

amortization_years.description: Amortization in years with monthly payments; 0 means interest-only. Any balance outstanding at the horizon is repaid from sale proceeds.

operating_expenses_annual.description: Year-1 operating expenses borne by the owner (utilities, repairs, management), USD per year.

capex_reserve_annual.description: Year-1 capital reserve, USD per year. Treated as a cash cost; not tax-deductible.

property_taxes_annual.description: Year-1 property taxes, USD per year.

insurance_annual.description: Year-1 property insurance, USD per year.

expense_growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth applied to expenses after year 1, e.g. 0.03 (year k = year-1 amount × (1 + g)^(k − 1)). Must be less than 1.

amount.description: Expected gross sale price at the end of the horizon, USD.

oneOf.description: A stated residual value.

cap_rate.description: Exit capitalization rate, e.g. 0.07. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

stabilized_noi.description: Stabilized NOI the property would earn if leased at market in the year after the horizon, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Residual = stabilized NOI ÷ exit cap rate (direct capitalization).

residual.description: How the sale price at the horizon is set.

selling_costs_rate.description: Brokerage and closing costs on sale as a share of the sale price, e.g. 0.03. Must be less than 1.

tax.description: Optional after-tax comparison. When omitted (the default), both cases are compared pre-tax. Operating expenses, property taxes, and insurance are always deductible when this block is present; the gain on sale is taxed at the marginal rate (no separate recapture rate).

marginal_tax_rate.description: Combined marginal income tax rate applied to deductions and to the gain on sale, e.g. 0.26. Must be less than 1.

depreciation_life_years.description: Straight-line depreciation life for the building (39 for US non-residential real property). No mid-month convention.

land_share.description: Share of purchase price plus closing costs allocated to land, which is not depreciated. Must be less than 1.

rent_deductible.description: Whether rent paid in the lease case is deductible (true for an operating business).

interest_deductible.description: Whether loan interest in the own case is deductible.

depreciation_deductible.description: Whether depreciation in the own case is deductible.

tools.name: calc_multifamily_rent_roll
tools.title: Multifamily rent roll
tools.description: Analyze an apartment rent roll (up to 5,000 units with status occupied, notice, vacant, model, or down; market and lease rent per month; lease dates; concessions as weeks free, months free, or dollars): gross potential rent, vacancy, non-revenue units, loss to lease, concessions amortised straight-line over each lease term, effective rent income, physical and economic occupancy, effective rent per unit and per SF, a lease expiration schedule by month, and a per-unit-type summary. Single-lease mode (lease instead of units) returns the effective monthly rent after a weeks-free or months-free concession. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.multifamily_rent_roll@1, every step, and any warnings.

as_of.description: Rent roll date, YYYY-MM-DD. Required with units: leases that ended before it are month-to-month, and expirations are scheduled from it.

units.description: Rent roll mode: every unit in the property, one row each (up to 5,000). Give units or lease, not both.

unit_id.description: Unit number or ID as on the rent roll, e.g. "101".

unit_type.description: Floor plan or type, e.g. "1x1" or "A2". Groups the per-type summary; defaults to the bedroom count.

bedrooms.description: Bedrooms (0 = studio). Used to group units when unit_type is absent.

sf.description: Unit square feet. Needed for per-SF figures. Must be greater than 0.

status.description: occupied (leased and in place), notice (leased, the resident has given notice to vacate), vacant, model, or down (offline). Occupied and notice units are leased; model and down units are non-revenue.

market_rent.description: Market (asking) rent per month for the unit, USD.

lease_rent.description: Contract (lease) rent per month, USD, before concessions. Required for occupied and notice units; ignored for vacant, model, and down units.

lease_end.description: Lease end date (last day), YYYY-MM-DD. A lease that ended before as_of is month-to-month.

lease_term_months.description: Lease term in months for amortising the concession, e.g. 12. Defaults to the term from lease_start to lease_end. Must be greater than 0.

weeks.description: Weeks of free rent, e.g. 6. Must be greater than 0.

oneOf.description: Weeks free: worth lease_rent × 12 ÷ 52 per week (a week of a year's rent).

months.description: Months of free rent, e.g. 1 or 1.5. Must be greater than 0.

oneOf.description: Months free: worth lease_rent × months.

amount.description: Total concession over the lease in USD, e.g. a $500 look-and-lease credit.

oneOf.description: A dollar concession for the whole lease.

concession.description: Concession on this lease: weeks_free, months_free, or a dollar amount. Amortised straight-line over the lease term; needs lease_term_months or lease_start and lease_end.

lease.description: Single-lease mode: the effective monthly rent of one lease after a weeks-free, months-free, or dollar concession. Give units or lease, not both.

lease_rent.description: Contract (lease) rent per month, USD, before concessions.

market_rent.description: Market (asking) rent per month, USD, for the loss to lease. Optional.

sf.description: Unit square feet, for effective rent per SF. Optional. Must be greater than 0.

lease_end.description: Lease end date (last day), YYYY-MM-DD. A lease that ended before as_of is month-to-month.

lease_term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 12. Give this, or lease_start and lease_end. Must be greater than 0.

concession.description: Concession: weeks_free, months_free, or a dollar amount, amortised straight-line over the term. Omit for none.

weeks.description: Weeks of free rent, e.g. 6. Must be greater than 0.

oneOf.description: Weeks free: worth lease_rent × 12 ÷ 52 per week (a week of a year's rent).

months.description: Months of free rent, e.g. 1 or 1.5. Must be greater than 0.

oneOf.description: Months free: worth lease_rent × months.

amount.description: Total concession over the lease in USD, e.g. a $500 look-and-lease credit.

oneOf.description: A dollar concession for the whole lease.

include_units.description: Rent roll mode: include a per-unit table with loss to lease, amortised concession, and effective rent (can be long).

tools.name: calc_net_effective_rent
tools.title: Net effective rent (NER)
tools.description: Compute effective rent, straight-line net effective rent, and discounted net effective rent ($/SF/yr) after free rent, TI allowance, leasing commissions, and other landlord concessions. Rent is monthly in advance from the commencement day (no calendar proration), discounted at annual rate ÷ 12. schedule.unit (kw, mw, unit, acre, key, room, space) reports $/kW/yr, $/acre/yr and so on instead of $/SF/yr. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.net_effective_rent@1, every step, and any warnings.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

area_sf.description: Rentable square feet, or the quantity leased in unit (kW, MW, units, acres, keys, rooms, spaces) when unit is set. Must be greater than 0.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5; per unit per year when unit is set (a $/kW/month quote × 12).

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound. Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year (or per unit per year when unit is set) added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

unit.description: What area_sf and the per-SF fields measure: sf (default, square feet), kw or mw (data-center critical load), unit (apartment or other unit), acre (ground or yard lease), key or room (hotel), or space (parking). Every number is computed exactly as for square feet; the unit changes labels, steps, and warnings and adds unit and rate_unit to the result. Fields keep their _sf and _psf names: with unit kw, area_sf holds kW and starting_rent_psf_annual holds $/kW/yr. Omit for square feet.

schedule.description: The lease's base-rent terms (same input as calc_rent_schedule).

ti_allowance_psf.description: Landlord-funded tenant improvement allowance, USD per SF (per schedule.unit when set), paid once at commencement (not per year).

leasing_commissions.description: Total leasing commissions paid by landlord, USD.

other_concessions.description: Any other landlord concessions paid at commencement (moving allowance, buyout), USD.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12); 0 gives the undiscounted (straight-line) NER. Must be less than 1.

tools.name: calc_npv
tools.title: Net present value
tools.description: NPV of periodic cash flows (t = 0, 1, 2, ...; the t = 0 flow is not discounted) at a per-period discount rate given as a decimal. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.npv@1, every step, and any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Periodic cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, …; negative for outflows (e.g. purchase price at t = 0). At most 10000.

rate.description: Discount rate per period as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 for 8%. Match the cash-flow period: for monthly flows pass the monthly rate (e.g. 0.06 ÷ 12 = 0.005). Must be greater than -1.

tools.name: calc_percentage_rent
tools.title: Retail percentage rent
tools.description: Percentage (overage) rent for a lease year: net sales after exclusions over a natural or fixed breakpoint, prorated for partial years, less amounts already paid. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.percentage_rent@1, every step, and any warnings.

gross_sales.description: Gross sales reported for the lease year (or partial year), USD.

sales_exclusions.description: Sales excluded by the lease (returns, sales tax, gift cards, employee sales, …), USD.

rate.description: Percentage rent rate, e.g. 0.06 for 6%. Must be greater than 0. Must be less than 1.

base_rent_annual.description: Annual base rent, USD per year (a full lease year, even for a partial period); used for the natural breakpoint.

breakpoint.description: Breakpoint above which percentage rent applies. Default: natural.

oneOf.description: Natural breakpoint = annual base rent ÷ rate.

amount.description: Annual sales breakpoint stated in the lease, USD.

oneOf.description: Artificial (fixed) breakpoint stated in the lease.

period_fraction.description: Fraction of a full lease year covered (e.g. 0.5 for a six-month partial year). Prorates the breakpoint. Must be greater than 0.

percentage_rent_paid.description: Percentage rent already paid during the period, USD.

tools.name: calc_prepayment_and_defeasance
tools.title: Loan prepayment premium and defeasance
tools.description: Prepayment premium, total payoff, and cost as a share of balance for a fixed-rate amortizing or interest-only loan under yield maintenance (PV of remaining payments or rate differential, with a minimum and an explicit discounting convention), a step-down schedule, a flat percentage, or defeasance (cost of the securities portfolio that funds the remaining payments plus stated costs). Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.prepayment_and_defeasance@1, every step, and any warnings.

balance.description: Outstanding principal balance at the payoff date, USD. Must be greater than 0.

note_rate_annual.description: Fixed annual note rate, e.g. 0.055. Must be less than 1.

remaining_term_months.description: Months from the payoff date to the loan's maturity date (the balloon is due with the final payment).

amortization_months.description: Remaining amortization basis in months at the payoff date (e.g. 300 for a 30-year schedule with 5 years elapsed); 0 for interest-only. Must be at least remaining_term_months.

accrued_interest.description: Accrued but unpaid interest to the payoff date, USD; added to the total payoff.

treasury_rate_annual.description: Yield on the reference Treasury (usually the one maturing closest to the loan's maturity), e.g. 0.041. Must be less than 1.

spread_annual.description: Spread added to the Treasury yield for discounting, e.g. 0.005 when the note says 'Treasury plus 50 basis points'. Default 0 (Treasury flat). Must be less than 1.

minimum_pct.description: Minimum premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.01 for a 1% floor (default). 0 for no floor. Must be less than 1.

basis.description: pv_of_payments (default): premium = PV of the remaining scheduled payments at the discount rate − balance. rate_differential: premium = PV of (note rate − discount rate) ÷ 12 × scheduled balance for each remaining month.

discount_convention.description: Compounding convention for the discount rate. monthly (default): monthly rate = annual ÷ 12. semiannual: annual is a bond-equivalent yield, monthly rate = (1 + annual ÷ 2)^(1/6) − 1. Lenders differ; read the note.

oneOf.description: Yield maintenance.

loan_month.description: Loan month (1 = first month after origination) in which the payoff occurs.

through_month.description: Last loan month in which this percentage applies.

pct.description: Premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.05 for 5%. Must be less than 1.

schedule.description: Step-down schedule in ascending through_month order, e.g. 5-4-3-2-1. After the last through_month the loan is open (0%).

oneOf.description: Step-down (declining percentage) premium.

pct.description: Premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.02. Must be less than 1.

oneOf.description: Flat percentage premium.

anyOf.description: One flat annual yield for all replacement securities. Must be less than 1.

months.description: Months from the payoff date up to and including which this yield applies; points in ascending order.

rate.description: Annual yield on replacement securities maturing at or before that month, e.g. 0.042. Must be less than 1.

anyOf.description: Yield curve as a step function: each payment uses the first point whose months ≥ its month; beyond the last point, the last rate.

replacement_yield.description: Yield on the government securities bought to fund the remaining payments: a flat annual rate, or a list of {months, rate} points.

costs.description: Stated transaction costs, USD: defeasance consultant, legal, accountant, rating agency, servicer and custodian fees.

discount_convention.description: Compounding convention for the discount rate. monthly (default): monthly rate = annual ÷ 12. semiannual: annual is a bond-equivalent yield, monthly rate = (1 + annual ÷ 2)^(1/6) − 1. Lenders differ; read the note.

oneOf.description: Defeasance: buy securities that replicate the remaining payments.

tools.name: calc_reconcile_cam
tools.title: Tie out CAM reconciliations against another system's results
tools.description: Reconcile FactLot's CAM reconciliation for one expense pool with another system's per-tenant results (Yardi or any other; parity is not claimed and is untested against a real export): give the calc_cam_reconciliation_batch input plus, per tenant, what the other system reported (share, gross-up, cap limit and reduction, admin fee, base-year or stop deduction, billed amount, estimates, balance; billed_amount required) and a tolerance. Returns per tenant and line FactLot's amount, the other amount, the difference and whether it is within tolerance, tenants missing on either side, and likely causes worded as hypotheses to check: a different pro rata share (and, when every share differs by one factor, the pool's denominator), or a FactLot rerun that matches the other system with lines left to the default controllable: true set uncontrollable, the cap's base year one year off, the other cap method, the other gross-up target or no gross-up, the admin fee before or after and within or outside the cap, or no fee on uncontrollable lines; and differing estimates paid. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.reconcile_cam@1, every step, and any warnings.

year.description: Calendar or lease year being reconciled.

category.description: Expense line as named in the operating statement, e.g. "janitorial".

amount.description: Building-level actual expense for the year, USD.

controllable.description: Subject to the cap. Taxes, insurance, and utilities are typically uncontrollable. Default true; under a cap, lines left unset are named in warnings.

recoverable.description: Excluded expenses (capital items, landlord-only costs) are dropped entirely.

variable.description: Varies with occupancy, so eligible for gross-up (janitorial, utilities, management fee). Default false; with a gross-up, lines left unset are named in warnings.

admin_fee_applies.description: Included in the admin_fee base. Set false for lines the lease excludes from the fee (often taxes, insurance, utilities, or a management fee already charged).

expenses.description: The building's operating expense pool for the year, entered once for every tenant: category, amount, controllable, recoverable, variable, admin_fee_applies.

gross_up.description: Gross up variable expenses to the target occupancy when actual occupancy is lower. Omit if the lease has no gross-up.

actual_occupancy.description: Average occupancy for the year, e.g. 0.82. Must be greater than 0.

target_occupancy.description: Gross-up occupancy stated in the lease (commonly 0.95 or 1.0). Must be greater than 0.

name.description: Tenant or suite label, unique, e.g. "Suite 200 – Acme".

pro_rata_share.description: Tenant's pro rata share, 0 < share ≤ 1 (e.g. 12,000 / 150,000 = 0.08). Must be greater than 0.

structure.description: Expense structure from the lease. Default: net.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its full share of recoverable expenses (NNN / net).

base_year_expenses.description: Total building recoverable expenses in the base year, already grossed up, USD.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over base-year expenses.

stop_amount.description: Building-level expense stop, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over a fixed expense stop.

cap.description: Cap on the tenant's share of controllable expenses. Omit if the lease has no cap.

method.description: compounding_from_base: reference × (1+rate)^years (often called cumulative, compounding). simple_from_base: reference × (1 + rate × years) (cumulative, non-compounding). year_over_year: prior year's capped amount × (1+rate) (non-cumulative). Map the lease language to one of these explicitly.

rate.description: Annual cap as a decimal, e.g. 0.05. Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

reference_amount.description: Tenant's share of controllable expenses in the reference year: the base year for *_from_base, or the prior year's capped amount for year_over_year, USD.

years_elapsed.description: Years since the base year (required for `*_from_base`).

admin_fee.description: Administrative fee the lease adds to the tenant's share. Omit if the lease has none.

rate.description: Administrative or management fee as a decimal of the fee base, e.g. 0.15 for 15%. The base is the tenant's share of recoverable lines with admin_fee_applies (after gross-up). Must be greater than -1. Must be less than 10.

applied.description: Fee on controllable lines computed on the tenant's share before the cap (before_cap) or on the capped amount (after_cap). Fees on uncontrollable lines are never capped. Irrelevant without a cap.

capped.description: True when the fee on controllable lines counts toward the controllable cap (controllable share plus fee may not exceed the cap limit); false adds it outside the cap.

occupancy.description: Partial-year occupancy: the tenant's share, cap limit, and base-year or stop deduction are prorated by occupied days ÷ period days (both inclusive), so a full-year cap and base are not applied to a part year. Omit for a full year.

move_in_date.description: Date the tenant's share starts within the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_start_date.

move_out_date.description: Last day of the tenant's share within the period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_end_date.

period_start_date.description: First day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to January 1 of year; set it for a lease year.

period_end_date.description: Last day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days after the start). Defaults to December 31 of year.

estimates_paid.description: Estimated CAM payments the tenant made during the year, USD (total for the year, not monthly).

excluded_categories.description: Expense categories this tenant's lease excludes, treated as recoverable: false for this tenant only. Each must match a category in expenses.

admin_fee_excluded_categories.description: Expense categories this tenant's lease keeps out of the admin fee base, treated as admin_fee_applies: false for this tenant only. Each must match a category in expenses.

tenants.description: Every tenant to reconcile (up to 500): each one's share, structure (base year or stop), cap, admin fee, occupancy, estimates paid, and lease-specific exclusions. Each statement equals calc_cam_reconciliation for that tenant.

cam.description: The FactLot CAM input for one expense pool, exactly as calc_cam_reconciliation_batch takes it (the same pool, shares and lease terms you entered in the other system).

system.description: Name of the system or file the results come from, echoed in the result, e.g. "Yardi CAM recon export" (free text).

pool.description: The pool these results are for, e.g. "CAM", echoed in the result.

tenant.description: Tenant as the other system names it; matched to cam.tenants[].name exactly, else ignoring case and punctuation.

pool.description: The other system's expense pool for this row, e.g. "CAM" (echoed; reconcile one pool per call).

pro_rata_share.description: The other system's pro rata share for the tenant, 0 < share ≤ 1. Must be greater than 0.

gross_up_applied.description: Whether the other system grossed up variable expenses for this tenant.

grossed_up_expenses.description: The other system's pool after gross-up (the building amount before the tenant's share), USD.

cap_applied.description: Whether a cap reduced the other system's charge.

cap_limit.description: The other system's cap limit on the tenant's controllable share, USD.

cap_reduction.description: Amount the cap removed in the other system, USD.

admin_fee_applied.description: Whether the other system charged an admin fee.

tools.name: calc_tx_unequal_appraisal
tools.title: Texas unequal appraisal: median of adjusted comparables
tools.description: Evidence calculation only: not an appraisal or an opinion of value, not legal or tax advice, and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. The arithmetic of Tex. Tax Code §41.43(b)(3) and §42.26(a)(3), the subject's value against the median appraised value of a reasonable number of comparable properties appropriately adjusted. Takes 3–200 comparables chosen by the caller, each with its roll value and the caller's adjustments (percent, USD amount, or $/SF, each with a reason); optionally normalizes each comparable to value per SF of improvement or land area times the subject's area; applies percentages summed or compounded, then amounts; and returns every comparable's normalized and adjusted value, the sorted list, the median (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values), and the subject's value minus the median in USD (subject_minus_median) and as a fraction of the median (subject_minus_median_pct: 0.1554 means 15.54%, a decimal like every rate in FactLot, not 0.1554%), with the statutes cited. Warns on mixed value bases, §42.26(d) and the §23.231 limitation, comparables in another county, fewer than 5 comparables, total adjustments over 25%, a comparable identical to the subject, no adjustments at all (the median is then unadjusted), and, with normalize_by none, a comparable whose area differs from the subject's by more than 25%. Each comparable row carries flags (code and sentence, facts about the inputs, never a reason the tool drops anything): value per SF more than twice or less than half the subject's, a land-to-improvement area ratio more than twice or less than half the subject's, an area the subject has but the comparable lacks. Optional label (up to 80 characters) and address (up to 120) on the subject and each comparable are echoed in the result (subject_label, subject_address, comparables[i].label and .address) for reports. registry_tx_equity_candidates returns calc_args, its candidates in this tool's input shape, for the caller to review and edit before calling this tool. It does not choose comparables, invent adjustments, or say whether to protest. Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same result, with formula ID calc.tx_unequal_appraisal@1, every step, and any warnings.

tools.description: Prepare the standard statements of a tenant estoppel certificate from verified lease facts, for a lender or buyer who wants the tenant to confirm the lease.
