tools.name: fact_package_send
tools.title: Send a fact package to a counterparty for confirmation
tools.description: Send a fact package to another firm for confirmation through the FactLot record, and get back a link for them. For an expense (CAM) reconciliation: the tenant's facts (lease terms and the landlord's statement figures, each with its quote and page, from doc_verify_facts or doc_abstract_lease) go in a package from fact_package_create, the arithmetic is calc_cam_reconciliation's output as calculation, and each line is an item: accept_theirs where the sender accepts the counterparty's figure, state_ours where the lease gives a different figure and the counterparty is asked to agree or dispute it. The counterparty opens the link on a plain web page (no account needed), sees every item with both figures, the quote, page and document fingerprint, and agrees or disputes each. Every accepted or agreed item is recorded as a reliance, citing the package digest. The FactLot record keeps each fact, its quote, the page and each document's SHA-256, never the documents. A send goes to an outside party and cannot be recalled. Refuses without approved_by, the full name of the person who reviewed every item, and approval_confirmed: true. Refuses a package that fails fact_package_verify's integrity checks, and an item whose fact_ids are not in the package. Real or test: a package is sent for real only through the hosted FactLot API with the subscription's own FactLot key (paid, or an email-confirmed free key) or a connection signed in with one; a real send records reliances between the named organisations at once. Every other call is a test (no key, a free connection without a key, a guest key, or a local or self-hosted FactLot): the counterparty can still open the link and answer, but nothing is recorded as a reliance or counted in the FactLot record's measure. The answer says which happened (recorded_as, test_mode, and message with the reason). Returns the package id, digest, link_for_counterparty, status_link_for_sender (private to the sender) and what was recorded. For a tenant estoppel (kind estoppel) the items are the statements from estoppel_prepare package_items, every one state_ours: the tenant confirms each, or states its own version, on the same page; the tenant gives the signer's full name and title and signs electronically on the same page (a consent statement ticked and the name typed): the FactLot record keeps the signer, the time in UTC, the consent wording's version and a SHA-256 over the answered statements, and no IP address. relying_parties gives a lender or buyer its own view link (links_for_relying_parties), which shows the statements, the tenant's answers, the signature and the document fingerprints and lets that firm record its own reliance, one per confirmed statement and never on a disputed one, and only after the tenant has signed; where any statement is disputed, the page lists each with the tenant's own version and the firm must acknowledge them first, and the reliance stores which statements were confirmed and which disputed at that moment. The relying firm must differ from the sender and the tenant. With attestation (from audit_expense_statement, estoppel_prepare or rent_roll_certify on the hosted API) the FactLot record checks the service's signature and that the items, grades, figures and facts are the ones the service computed, and records the package as attested; a package with none is recorded as unattested, and a package with an attestation that does not verify is refused. Where the FactLot record requires it, a real package of kind expense_reconciliation, estoppel or rent_roll must be attested; test packages need not be. The answer says which (attestation.status and its line). fact_package_status reads the answers and the reliers later.

package.description: The package from fact_package_create (signed or not).

kind.description: What is being confirmed. estoppel: the statements from estoppel_prepare, answered by the tenant and then open to a lender or buyer through relying_parties. rent_roll: a certified rent roll from rent_roll_certify, asserted by the sender (no answer step) and open at once to the lender or buyer named in to, and to relying_parties, who record reliance on each line graded as matching.

label.description: What it is about, in words (for example an address).

subject.description: The property or lease the facts are about.

email.description: Kept by FactLot to reach the person; never shown to the other party.
Kept by FactLot; never shown to anyone else.

key.description: A short stable name for the item, unique in the package.

label.description: What the item is, in plain words the counterparty will read.

value.description: The sender's figure. For accept_theirs it is the figure the sender accepts (the counterparty's own); for state_ours it is the figure the sender says is right.

position.description: accept_theirs: the sender accepts the counterparty's figure (recorded at once as relied on by the sender). state_ours: the sender states its own figure and asks the counterparty to agree or dispute it.

their_value.description: The counterparty's figure, when it differs (always give it for state_ours).

fact_ids.description: The ids of the facts in the package this item rests on. Each fact must carry a source quote, page and document sha256. Only an estoppel statement the tenant alone can confirm (tenant_to_confirm true) may have none.

note.description: A sentence on why, shown to the counterparty.

number.description: Estoppel: the statement's number in the certificate.

text.description: Estoppel: the statement as the tenant reads and answers it (estoppel_prepare package_items[].text).

tenant_to_confirm.description: Estoppel: true for a statement with no lease source that only the tenant can confirm. It has no fact_ids.

needs_tenant_value.description: Estoppel: true when the tenant must state the figure or date itself (for example the date rent is paid through); the tenant's answer then carries its own version.

grade.description: Rent roll: the line's grade from rent_roll_certify. Reliance is recorded only for matches_lease and matches_lease_confirmed_by_tenant.

grade_label.description: Rent roll: the grade in words, as rent_roll_certify gives it.

differences.description: Rent roll: the fields of the line that differ.

against.description: The figure it was compared with.

against_label.description: What it was compared with: Lease, Tenant or Roll.

difference.description: Roll minus the figure compared with.

estoppel_package_id.description: Rent roll: the estoppel package whose confirmed statements back a matches_lease_confirmed_by_tenant grade.

estoppel_statements.description: Rent roll: the keys of the estoppel statements the tenant agreed.

items.description: The line items. The counterparty answers each state_ours item.

calculation.description: A calc tool's output (for example calc_cam_reconciliation) shown to the counterparty with every step.

relying_parties.description: Estoppel and rent_roll only: a label for each lender or buyer that is to get its own view link and token (for example the lender's name). Each can read the package and record its own reliance; none can answer for the tenant. For an estoppel with none given FactLot makes one link; for a rent roll the party named in to has a link already and these are additional.

estoppel_links.description: Rent roll only: the sender's status link (status_link_for_sender) of each estoppel that backs a matches_lease_confirmed_by_tenant line. The FactLot record opens each with its private token to check the tenant agreed the statements; the token is not stored.

attestation.description: The attestation that the hosted FactLot service returned with package_items from audit_expense_statement, estoppel_prepare or rent_roll_certify, passed unchanged. The FactLot record checks the service's signature and that the items, grades, figures and facts sent are the ones the service computed. Without it the package is recorded as unattested.

approved_by.description: The full name of the person at the sender who reviewed every item and approved sending this package. Recorded with the package and shown to the counterparty.

approval_confirmed.description: Confirms that the person named in approved_by reviewed every item, both figures, the quote and page behind each, the calculation and the recipient, and approved sending. The tool refuses unless it is true.

tools.name: fact_package_status
tools.title: Read a sent fact package's status and answers
tools.description: Read the status of a package sent with fact_package_send: for each item, whether the counterparty agreed or disputed it (with their reason and who answered), which items the sender accepted, the reliances recorded, and the package's integrity. For an estoppel it also gives the statement number and text, the tenant's own version where it gave one, the signer's name and title with the electronic signature record (time in UTC, consent wording version and text, SHA-256 of the signed statements, and whether they are unchanged), reliers (each lender or buyer that recorded reliance, its role, the statements and when), and for each relying-party link the first and last time it was opened and how many times, with the name, firm and role given once reliance is recorded and the statements confirmed and disputed at that moment. Give the sender's private status_link (or package_id with token). Needs no account and costs nothing; it reads only your own package, and the counterparty's link cannot read it. The answer also gives attestation (attested or unattested, with the line the pages show: computed by FactLot and unchanged since, or not verified) and package_signature (the outcome of checking the signature fact_package_create's holder made, when there is one). The answer says whether the package was sent in test mode (test_mode true: it does not count in the FactLot record's measure) or for real.

status_link.description: The sender's private status link from fact_package_send.

token.description: The sender's private token (with package_id), if there is no link.

tools.name: fact_package_verify
tools.title: Verify a fact package
tools.description: Verify a fact package from fact_package_create: recompute every fact's hash, the Merkle root and the digest from the content (any changed fact, title, date or document list shows as a mismatch); check each fact against fact_validate; check the Ed25519 signature, against the public_key you pass (base64url, the signer's key you trust) or, without one, only against the key inside the package (which proves nothing about who signed); and, given the source documents' pages, check every quote is on its cited page. Returns valid plus each check's details, checks_run and checks_not_run (what was and was not checked), and values_not_checked: the parts of extracted facts' values that their quotes do not confirm (a true/false value, an enum, a summary), which do not change valid. Not checked: that the pages you pass are the original files (pass sha256 to tie them to the file hash), or what the facts mean.

package.description: A fact package from fact_package_create, signed or not.

public_key.description: The signer's Ed25519 public key you trust: 32 bytes as base64url (a JWK's x). With it the signature must verify for the package to be valid.

documents.description: Optional: the source documents' pages (with sha256 when the facts cite the file's hash). Each fact's quote is then checked on its cited page.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

tools.name: fact_validate
tools.title: Validate a FactLot fact
tools.description: Check one FactLot fact against the published fact schema (spec/schemas/fact.json): subject URN, dotted predicate, as_of date, provenance, optional rights; unknown fields are rejected at every level. Rules: every fact except a computed one cites at least one source (an inferred fact cites the evidence it was inferred from); a computed fact names its formula or cites a source; valid_from is not after valid_to; a source span does not end before it starts. For Ingest predicates (lease.expiration_date, lease.rentable_area_sf, lease.base_rent_schedule, ...) the value must have the predicate's shape and every source quote must state the value, by the same written-form rules as doc_verify_facts (a quote saying "2,500 square feet" does not support 1000). Not checked: that the quote is in the document, that the document or sha256 exists, that supersedes IDs exist, and quotes for other predicates; doc_verify_facts with the document's pages checks the quote. Returns { valid, issues }. Meant for checking facts before they are stored or shared.

fact.description: A FactLot fact: subject, predicate, value, as_of, provenance (with sources), optional rights.

tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch a FactLot knowledge document
tools.description: Fetch the full text of a FactLot knowledge document by the id returned from search. With a registry loaded, a registry fact's source document_id (fl:document:sha256-…) returns that source snapshot: publisher, dataset, URL, retrieval date, as-of date, licence, AI-use and redistribution rights, file name and size.

id.description: Document id from search, e.g. tool:calc_cam_reconciliation, or a registry source snapshot's FactLot document ID (fl:document:sha256-…) when a registry is loaded.

tools.name: id_building
tools.title: FactLot building ID
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a building from its street address: county FIPS, ZIP code, and street line. Every condominium unit, suite, and floor at the address gets the same building ID, offline. id_space takes it for a suite, and registry_get shows the building's parcels.

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS code, e.g. "11" for the District of Columbia.

zip.description: 5-digit ZIP code of the address, e.g. "20002" (ZIP+4 accepted).

street.description: Street line: house number and street, e.g. "208 Massachusetts Ave NE". A suite, unit or floor is ignored, and so is anything after a comma (city, state).

tools.name: id_document
tools.title: FactLot document ID
tools.description: Content-addressed FactLot ID (SHA-256) for a document such as a lease, amendment, or estoppel.

content_base64.description: Base64 of the exact file bytes (preferred: every party gets the same ID).

text.description: Document text, UTF-8 encoded before hashing. Use only when bytes are unavailable.

tools.name: id_entity
tools.title: FactLot legal-entity ID
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a legal entity (LLC, LP, corporation, trust) from its registry jurisdiction and file number, or from its LEI (an LEI whose ISO 17442 check digits do not match is rejected).

jurisdiction.description: Registry jurisdiction, e.g. "us-de" for Delaware, or "lei" for a Legal Entity Identifier.

registry_number.description: File number issued by that registry, or the 20-character LEI (its ISO 17442 check digits are verified).

tools.name: id_parcel
tools.title: FactLot parcel ID
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a parcel from state FIPS, county FIPS, and the assessor's parcel number (APN). The same parcel always yields the same ID, offline. It serves as the join key across systems. APNs that differ only in where a separator falls ("12-34", "1-234") get different IDs; in a county with a documented fixed-width format the variants of one APN converge (NYC BBL "3-1234-56" = "3012340056").

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS code, e.g. "06" for California.

county_fips.description: 3-digit county FIPS code, e.g. "037" for Los Angeles County.

apn.description: Assessor's parcel number exactly as the county prints it. Letter case and the separator characters are normalized; where a separator falls is kept, except in counties with a documented fixed-width format (NYC BBL, Los Angeles AIN, Cook County PIN, DC SSL).

tools.name: id_parse
tools.title: Parse a FactLot ID
tools.description: Validate a FactLot URN and return its kind, components, and short ID.

urn.description: A FactLot URN to validate, e.g. fl:parcel:us-06037:5432001012.

tools.name: id_space
tools.title: FactLot space (suite) ID
tools.description: FactLot ID for a suite or unit within a building, given the building's FactLot URN (from id_building). Suite designators are normalized: "Suite 100", "Ste 100" and "#100" agree, while "1-20" and "120" stay distinct.

building_urn.description: FactLot building URN from id_building, e.g. fl:building:us-11001:20002:208-massachusetts-ave-ne (a minted fl:building:<26-character token> also works).

suite.description: Suite or unit as written ("Suite 400", "STE 400", "#400", "3rd Floor" all normalize).

tools.name: lease_comp_search
tools.title: Search GSA lease comps (federal tenant)
tools.description: Search the 6,994 lease comps from the U.S. General Services Administration's Lease Inventory (October 2026 file, FactLot release lease-comps-gsa-2026-11-04), bundled with FactLot: works offline and on the hosted API, no registry needed. Caveat: the tenant in every one of these leases is the federal government (GSA, for an agency); they are not market comps for private tenants, and the rent is the current annual rent in GSA's file divided by the rentable SF, not the starting rent (no escalations, free rent, TI or commissions are known). Filter by state, 5-digit county FIPS, city, ZIP, a radius around a latitude/longitude (GSA's own coordinates; nothing is geocoded), rentable SF, commencement date, rent per SF, property type (office, industrial, other) and expense basis; sort; limit (default 25, at most 200). Each comp gives its FactLot lease ID, GSA lease number, address, county FIPS, building ID, landlord (organisations only; individuals are never stored), rentable SF, commencement, expiration, term, early-termination date, annual rent, rent per SF per year, property type, expense basis and the row of the GSA file it comes from. summary gives the count and the median, quartiles and range of rent per SF over every match, labelled as statistics of GSA leases. Every answer carries the caveat and the citation (GSA file URL, SHA-256 document ID, as-of and retrieval dates, licence: public domain). These are statistics of GSA leases, kept apart from market comps.

state.description: Two-letter state or territory code, e.g. "TX".

county_fips.description: 5-digit county FIPS code (state + county), e.g. "48201" for Harris County, Texas. Connecticut uses its planning regions (09110 to 09190).

city.description: City as GSA writes it, matched whole and ignoring case, e.g. "Houston".

near.description: Comps within a radius of a point, by great-circle distance to the coordinates GSA's file gives for each lease (FactLot geocodes nothing; give the point's coordinates yourself). Comps without coordinates are left out and counted in warnings.

radius_miles.description: Radius in miles (at most 500). Must be greater than 0.

min_rent_psf_yr.description: Lowest current rent, USD per rentable SF per year (GSA's current annual rent divided by the RSF).

max_rent_psf_yr.description: Highest current rent, USD per rentable SF per year.

property_type.description: office, industrial (GSA warehouse) or other (GSA special space): the largest use in the lease.

sort.description: Order of results: distance_asc (the default with near; needs near), commencement_desc (the default otherwise), commencement_asc, expiration_asc, expiration_desc, rent_psf_desc, rent_psf_asc, rentable_sf_desc, rentable_sf_asc. Ties go by GSA lease number.

limit.description: Maximum comps returned (1–200, default 25); the summary covers every match.

tools.name: lease_comp_validate
tools.title: Validate a lease comp and derive its NER
tools.description: Check a lease comparable one firm shares with others, as a FactLot fact with predicate lease.comp, and derive its net effective rent. The fact goes through fact_validate (schema, citations, rights), then the comp's own rules: shape (spec/schemas/fact.json LeaseComp: area, commencement, term or expiration, starting or current rent, escalation, free rent, TI, leasing commissions, expense basis, confirming party, verification), an expiration after commencement, a term that matches the dates, free rent within the term, no email, phone or ID number in the text. A comp names no person or company. With the default share profile it also needs the deal's starting rent, escalations, free rent, TI, property type, an expense basis other than unknown, and stated rights. When valid and a starting rent is given, ner.fact is a computed lease.net_effective_rent fact (formula calc.net_effective_rent@1, straight-line and discounted at discount_rate_annual, on the comp's own expense basis; no conversion between full service and net). Returns { valid, issues, warnings, ner }. Meant for checking a comp before it is shared.

fact.description: A FactLot fact with predicate lease.comp: subject (an fl:lease: URN), value (the comp), as_of, provenance (with at least one source: your own record is fine, cited by document_id or sha256 without sharing it), and rights (ai_use and redistribution).

profile.description: share (default): a comp offered to other firms: needs the deal's starting rent, escalations, free rent, TI, expense basis, property type, a term and stated rights. observed: a rent seen in a public record (current_rent_psf_yr is enough); no NER is derived without a starting rent.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate for the discounted NER (an assumption, not part of the comp). 0 gives the straight-line NER only. Must be less than 1.

tools.name: registry_coverage
tools.title: What the registry holds
tools.description: The counties (with parcel and building counts), entity registries, and crosswalk systems this FactLot Registry file holds, each with its sources and as-of dates. A miss outside these regions means not loaded, not absent. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

fields.description: true: each county also carries fields, the share of its parcels with each fact group it holds and its roll years with their value types.

tools.name: registry_get
tools.title: Get a registry record
tools.description: Everything the FactLot Registry knows about a parcel, legal entity, or building: status, current cited facts (owner of record, situs address, property category, areas, values), ownership links, external IDs, and for a parcel the building it belongs to (condominium units roll up into one building). value_history (parcels) lists market and appraised value by tax year from every snapshot, newest first, each value cited; a tax year two snapshots value differently appears once per value. as_of gives the facts as they stood on a date. A parcel's recorded sales and documents (transaction.sale, transaction.deed, debt.mortgage_recorded, debt.mortgage_satisfaction_recorded; one fact each, newest first) are kept to the newest 50 in facts and in history; when there are more, recorded_facts_truncated gives what was kept and the totals by predicate with the years left out, and registry_recorded_facts reads them all. warnings flags area facts that look wrong (building area above 40 times the land area, a land area of 0); the facts themselves are as the source publishes them. A building record can carry debt.cmbs_loan facts (one per CMBS trust holding a note of its loan: balance, rate, maturity, payment status, servicer, special-servicing dates, NOI, DSCR) and an entity record can carry entity.parent facts (the SEC registrant that lists it as a subsidiary in Exhibit 21), each cited to its SEC filing. A miss says whether the county or entity registry is loaded. On the hosted API, a call without a Pro or Team key gets the current roll year only in value_history and history, and of a parcel's recorded sales and documents only the newest sale or deed, with the count and years of the rest (the answer says so); a Pro or Team key gets every year and the newest 50 recorded facts. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

urn.description: FactLot URN of a parcel, entity, or building, e.g. fl:parcel:us-48201:0011440000001 (Harris County, Texas) or fl:parcel:us-36061:1000020002 (Manhattan: a New York City borough-block-lot).

include_history.description: Also return every fact from every snapshot, superseded ones included (history lists current facts too; a source loaded once has no superseded facts).

as_of.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD): return the facts and ownership links current on that date, from the snapshots dated on or before it, instead of the latest. With include_history, history stops at that date. On the hosted API a dated lookup needs a Pro or Team key.

tools.name: registry_lookup_batch
tools.title: Look up many parcels (batch)
tools.description: Up to 50 parcels in any loaded state in one call (a loan tape, a broker's list, a client's accounts), each item naming one parcel by exactly one of: urn (a FactLot parcel URN); apn with state_fips and county_fips (3 digits), or with a 5-digit county_fips alone (as registry_resolve_parcel takes them); or address with the optional place fields registry_search_address takes (state, city, postal_code, county_fips). ref, your own row id, is echoed back. Each item is answered as the single tools answer it: registry_get for a URN, registry_resolve_parcel for an account, registry_search_address (20 results) for an address, then registry_get on the URN found. results lists one entry per item in input order (index, ref, by: urn, account or address, status): found gives parcel, a compact row: urn, label, record_status, account, property_category, use_code, improvement_area_sf, year_built, value (the newest roll year's entry of registry_get's value_history: tax_year, market and appraised value, as_of, value types, file and each value's citation), owner_of_record (the owner of record fact exactly as registry_get gives it, with the entity linked to it, or null; organisations only, natural persons are never stored), citations (each field's fact id, document id, locator and as-of date), sources (each cited document with its title, URI, read date, licence, ai_use and redistribution) and warnings; an address item also gives match (exact, and how many parcels the search returned). not_found gives message and coverage exactly as the single tool's miss gives them (the reason: county or state not loaded, street or house number not held); a URN not in the registry also carries registry_get's NotFound as error, with the same coverage registry_resolve_parcel gives for that county. An address is found when exactly one search result is exact, or when the search returned one parcel and it is in the place the address names; exact means the same street address and unit (the label's street line, normalized as the address index normalizes it, 'Street' = 'St', is the query's, a unit written as a bare number after the street counting as the unit, and both name the same unit or neither does) in the place the address names (when it names a city or ZIP code, in its text or the city and postal_code fields, the label has that ZIP code or city). Otherwise it is ambiguous, with reason: several_places (the address names no city or ZIP code and the results are in more than one county; a parcel is never picked across counties), same_address (several parcels have the address exactly: separate accounts at one address), place_differs (the one parcel found is not shown in the place named) or no_exact_match; candidates lists up to 5 of the search's result cards (the exact ones first; never an owner), with matches and a message. error gives the item's own error, so it does not fail the others: a wrong combination of fields (two of urn, apn and address, a field another mode takes, a missing county), a malformed or non-parcel URN, or an item the registry could not answer (RegistryUnavailable; after 5 such items the rest are not sent and say not attempted, and when no item at all is answered the whole call fails with RegistryUnavailable). An item whose fields fail the input schema (a wrong type, an unknown field, an empty ref, a URN over 500 characters) fails the whole call with InputError, uncharged. summary counts items, found, not_found, ambiguous and errors. On the hosted API this batch tool needs a Pro or Team key, and each item counts as the one call that identifies its parcel would count on its own (registry_resolve_parcel for an account or a URN, registry_search_address for an address): a found or ambiguous item counts one registry lookup; an item that finds nothing inside loaded coverage, a URN not in the registry included, is an answer that finds nothing (not counted up to an hourly limit, counted past it); a miss outside loaded coverage and an item with an error count

ref.description: Your own id for this row (a loan number, a client account), echoed back with its answer.

apn.description: Parcel or account number as the county prints it (see registry_resolve_parcel), with state_fips and county_fips.

county_fips.description: With apn: 3-digit county FIPS with state_fips, or 5 digits alone ("48201"). With address: keeps the search to that county (5 digits, or 3 with state).

address.description: Street address, e.g. '1200 Main St, Houston, TX 77002', searched as registry_search_address searches it.

state.description: With address: state, two letters or full name; keeps the search to that state.

city.description: With address: city; orders the matches, never filters.

postal_code.description: With address: ZIP code; orders the matches, never filters.

items.description: The parcels (1–50), each by exactly one of urn, apn (with its county) or address.

tools.name: registry_owned_by
tools.title: Parcels owned by an entity
tools.description: Commercial parcels currently linked to a legal entity as owner of record (inferred links carry a confidence), each with the building it belongs to, plus a per-building summary so condominium units count once per building. On the hosted API, a call without a Pro or Team key gets the first three parcels, with every row of each and their buildings (the answer says how many were left out in portfolio_withheld and portfolio_note); a Pro or Team key gets every parcel. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

tools.name: registry_recorded_facts
tools.title: Recorded sales and documents of a parcel
tools.description: Every recorded sale and document of a parcel (transaction.sale, transaction.deed, debt.mortgage_recorded, debt.mortgage_satisfaction_recorded), newest first in registry_get's order, each a whole fact with its citation, a page at a time. registry_get keeps the newest 50 of them (on the hosted API without a Pro or Team key, the newest sale or deed only); when it holds more, its recorded_facts_truncated gives the totals, and this tool reads the rest. predicate limits the page to one of the four. Pass next_cursor back as cursor for the next page; next_cursor is null on the last. totals counts each predicate's facts. A price or amount is as recorded, zero or nominal included; the sources do not say whether a sale was at arm's length. Parties are organisations only. On the hosted API this tool needs a Pro or Team key. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page.

tools.name: registry_resolve_external
tools.title: Resolve an external ID
tools.description: Find the FactLot URN for an ID from another system, e.g. system "sdat_account" (a Maryland SDAT account number), "hcad_account" (a Harris CAD account number), "nyc_bbl" (a New York City borough-block-lot), "la_ain" (a Los Angeles County Assessor ID number), "sf_parcel", "boston_pid", "denver_schednum" or "ct_cama_link". registry_coverage lists the systems a registry holds. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

system.description: Crosswalk system name, e.g. "sdat_account" (Maryland), "hcad_account" (Harris County, Texas) or "nyc_bbl" (New York City).

tools.name: registry_resolve_parcel
tools.title: Resolve a parcel in the registry
tools.description: Find a parcel's FactLot URN from state FIPS, county FIPS, and APN, if the registry holds it. A miss returns urn null with coverage: whether that county is loaded in this registry. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS, e.g. "48" for Texas, "36" for New York.

county_fips.description: 3-digit county FIPS, e.g. "201" for Harris County, Texas, or "061" for New York County (Manhattan).

apn.description: Parcel or account number as the county prints it: an appraisal district account number in Texas, a borough-block-lot (e.g. 1000020002) in New York City, an AIN in Los Angeles County, a parcel number in San Francisco, a PID in Boston, a schedule number in Denver, the CAMA link in Connecticut.

tools.name: registry_search_address
tools.title: Search parcels by address
tools.description: Find commercial parcels by situs address. Matches whole words of the street line (the part before the first comma), normalized: 'Street' = 'St', 'Northwest' = 'N.W.' = 'NW'; a suite, unit, '#' or floor is ignored. A numbered street matches however it is written ('Fifth Avenue' = '5th Ave' = '5 Avenue', 'Forty-Second St' = '42nd St'), and a house number matches a lot whose address is a range holding it ('350 5th Ave' finds '338-350 5 AVENUE'): a range whose ends are both odd or both even holds only the numbers of that parity, one side of the street, and one whose ends differ holds every number between. Give a house number ('1200 Main', '1200 Main St NW') or a street name with its type ('Main St'); a city or a part of a word alone matches nothing. Give the place after the first comma ('1200 Main St, Houston, TX 77002') or as state, city, postal_code and county_fips: a state named after a city (or given as state) keeps the answer to that state, and county_fips to that county, before the limit is applied; the ZIP code and the city only order the matches (same ZIP code first, then same city, then the rest) and never filter; a bare state with no city in the query, and suite, floor or box text, are ignored. Within each place group, matches of the street as written come first, then other spellings, then house-number ranges, an exact address first, then the parcel whose label names the unit the query names (a unit never filters), then by label; parcels sharing one label come largest improvement area first (a parcel the roll gives no improvement area after those it gives one), those the roll records as land only last, then in URN order. Each result carries what tells parcels at one address apart: the district's account or lot number, property category, use code, improvement area, land_only (true when the roll records an improvement area of 0, false when it records an improvement, null when it records neither), and the unit its label names; never an owner. When the query names a city or ZIP code, a result whose own label does not name it and whose county is outside every county that place lies in, in the result's state (from the US Census Bureau's city and ZIP code tables and the registry's own labels; a place the tables do not know there is not judged), carries place_differs: true, and when every result does, note says the matches are outside the counties the place lies in and place_counties lists them. No match returns coverage: what this registry holds (in the named state when there is one), and in reason and message why (a city or ZIP code that lies wholly in counties the registry does not hold is said first, with those counties and the ones held in that state; a city or ZIP code never filters, so that search still covered every county held): the state or county is not loaded, the street is not held, the house number is held but not with the query's other words, or the street is held but not that house number (with the nearest numbers held on it). Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

query.description: Street address ('1200 Main St, Houston, TX 77002'), or a house number and street words, or a street name with its type; the city, state and ZIP code after the first comma narrow and order the matches. Give query or address, not both.

address.description: The same as query (give one of the two).

state.description: State, two letters or full name ('TX', 'Texas'): keeps the answer to that state, as a state after the city in the query does; it replaces one named there.

postal_code.description: 5-digit ZIP code (or ZIP+4): matches with it come first; it never filters, since some rolls write ZIP codes wrongly. Replaces one named in the query.

county_fips.description: County FIPS code, 5 digits ('48201') or 3 with state ('201'): keeps the answer to that county, read from each parcel's URN.

tools.name: registry_tx_equity_candidates
tools.title: Texas unequal-appraisal candidates
tools.description: Candidate comparable parcels for a Texas unequal-appraisal comparison (Tax Code §41.43(b)(3)), from one tax year of the subject's appraisal district roll (the newest year whose roll gives the subject a value, or tax_year), with every field of the subject and the candidates read from that year's roll only: same county and tax year, the same state property category code, improvement area within area_band of the subject's, year built within year_band years when both are known; parcels sharing the subject's neighborhood code first (when the roll gives one), then its ZIP code, then the rest of the county if fewer than min_matches. Optional narrowing, off by default: same_building_class, same_local_use_code, local_use_codes. Each candidate and the subject carry their roll fields: id, apn (the district's account number), value and value_basis, value_per_sf (that value divided by the improvement area, to the cent: the roll's figures and one division, not an opinion of value), market and appraised value, improvement and land area, year built, state property category, local use code, neighborhood code, building class, situs address, tax year, and the citation of the value fact; the subject adds its value history by tax year. Separate land and improvement values are not returned. calc_args gives the same subject and candidates with exactly calc_tx_unequal_appraisal's input fields (tax_year, subject, comparables; id = the FactLot URN, label = the situs address, nulls left out, no adjustments): the candidate list under the default rule, not a selection by FactLot, for the caller to review and edit (remove, add or adjust comparables, each adjustment with a reason) before passing it to calc_tx_unequal_appraisal. Order of operations: registry_tx_equity_candidates, then the person's review, then calc_tx_unequal_appraisal with the reviewed calc_args, then report_create. selection echoes the rule, the effective parameters, the tax year and roll sources used, the files the compared values come from (compared_files: as-of date, and whether the file is dated before July 25 of the tax year, the certification date in Tax Code §26.01(a)), the subject's category, class, use code and area (subject_summary), each narrowing parameter and whether it was applied, how many parcels each step of the rule left (steps), the candidates counted by building class and by local use code with the subject's own beside them (class_counts, use_code_counts), and which tier each candidate came from; selection_rule restates the parameters used (tax year, category, area band and year band with their bounds, the subject summary, the narrowing applied, the step counts, counts per tier) with a notice that the list is the default rule's output (the default rule with the narrowing listed, when a narrowing was applied). Each candidate's citation.document_id names its entry in sources, which gives that snapshot's license, attribution, ai_use and redistribution, which apply to that candidate. Candidates under FactLot's default rule, a design choice, not a legal standard; a person decides which, if any, to use. For evidence calculations only: FactLot does not represent property owners, file protests, or advise whether to protest. Not an appraisal or an opinion of value (Tex. Occ. Code §1103.003(1)); not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Never returns owner names, mailing addresses, or ownership facts: ownership is outside this comparison and is not needed for it. Texas parcels only. Tarrant County is not served by the hosted registry while the publisher's terms for AI use are unclear. On the hosted API, a call without a Pro or Team key gets the current roll year only in the subject's value_history (the answer says so); the candidates are unchanged. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

tools.name: rent_roll_certify
tools.title: Certify a rent roll against the leases, line by line
tools.description: Certify a commercial rent roll for a lender or buyer: check each line of the roll, given as verified facts (each value with its verbatim quote and page from the rent roll document), against the leases' verified facts (and, where there is one, the answers of a confirmed estoppel), and grade it. Compares per line the tenant name, suite, rentable area, lease start and expiration, current base rent (per year, per month and per SF, the lease's worked from its rent schedule and area), next rent step, security deposit, free rent outstanding, renewal options and recoveries structure, wherever both the roll and a lease fact state it. Each line is graded: matches lease; matches lease and confirmed by tenant (the tenant agreed the premises, expiration and base rent statements of an estoppel); differs (both figures, the dollar difference and the quotes); no lease supplied; or not checkable, with the reason. A field no lease fact covers is not checked, never assumed. Totals: occupied and vacant area, occupancy, annual base rent as stated against as the leases yield and the difference, WALT (calc_walt, by area and by rent), rollover by year and top-tenant concentration. Flags: leases expiring within 12 months, tenants on the roll with no lease, leases with no roll line, rent on the roll above the lease, the roll's own arithmetic. Returns package_items and package_calculation for fact_package_send kind rent_roll. Deterministic, no model, no clock (as_of is an input). Facts and arithmetic, not legal, appraisal or lending advice: the certifying party's certification, not FactLot, is what the lender or buyer relies on, and FactLot checked the roll against the documents supplied only. On the hosted API the whole answer also carries attestation, the service's signature over the items, grades and figures that fact_package_send carries, so the FactLot record can show them as computed by FactLot and unchanged since; a service without a signing key returns none and says so. On the hosted API, callers without a Pro or Team key get the summary only (totals, key figures, grade counts, flags) and the answer says what is withheld. Each free, email-verified account (an fl_free_ key) gets one whole document in total across audit_expense_statement, estoppel_prepare and rent_roll_certify: that answer says so, and the report built from the same arguments is included for 24 hours; Pro and Team include every document with the monthly allowance.

tools.name: rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline
tools.title: Texas property tax protest deadline
tools.description: Deadline to file a Texas property tax protest with the appraisal review board: the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice of appraised value was delivered, rolled past weekends and Texas legal holidays, plus a conservative file-by date (the last business day on or before the unadjusted deadline). status says where as_of (default: today in US Central time; echoed in as_of) falls: not_yet_open before January 1 of the tax year, open from then through the deadline, passed after it; days_remaining counts the days to the deadline (null once passed), and once passed next_season gives the same rule for the next tax year (May 15 basis). notes says what the rule does not cover (late protests, other §41.44 deadlines, §25.25 corrections) and which sections to read. Returns the statute citations, the rule's verification status and a disclaimer. Information about a statutory deadline: not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Verification status: verified. The answer carries rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline@2 and the statutes it rests on.

notice_delivered_date.description: Date the appraisal district's notice of appraised value was delivered (Tax Code §25.19), YYYY-MM-DD. A mailed notice is presumed delivered on the day it was deposited in the mail (§1.07(c)). Omit if unknown (May 15 is then the only basis).

as_of.description: Date the status is measured from, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the current date in US Central time (America/Chicago), when the call is answered; pass it to fix the date (for a report, or for El Paso and Hudspeth counties, which keep Mountain time).

tools.name: rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline_batch
tools.title: Texas property tax protest deadlines (batch)
tools.description: Texas property tax protest deadlines for many notices in one call (1–200 items, e.g. a consultant's client list): each item's id, tax year and, if known, notice delivery date. Each result is exactly what rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline returns for that item under rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline@2 (deadline, unadjusted deadline, governing basis, conservative file-by date, skipped days, status, days_remaining, next_season, the item's warnings), echoed with its id; an item with invalid input carries its error and the others are still answered. One as_of (default: today in US Central time) applies to every item. summary counts the items per deadline, earliest first, with the earliest and latest deadline, and per status (by_status). The as_of used, the notes, the statute citations, the rule's verification status and the disclaimer appear once (value.as_of, value.notes, value.rule, value.disclaimer). A rules tool: never a registry lookup. Information about statutory deadlines: not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney; it does not say whether to protest. Verification status: verified. The answer carries rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline_batch@1 and the statutes it rests on.

id.description: Your label for this notice (a client, account or parcel number), echoed back with its result. Unique within the batch.

tax_year.description: Tax year being protested, e.g. 2026 (2000–2100). An invalid value is an error for this item only.

notice_delivered_date.description: Date the appraisal district's notice of appraised value was delivered (Tax Code §25.19), YYYY-MM-DD. A mailed notice is presumed delivered on the day it was deposited in the mail (§1.07(c)). Omit if unknown (May 15 is then the only basis). An invalid date is an error for this item only.

items.description: The notices to compute deadlines for (1–200): each one's id, tax year and, if known, notice delivery date. Each result equals rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline for that item.

as_of.description: Date the status is measured from, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the current date in US Central time (America/Chicago), when the call is answered; pass it to fix the date (for a report, or for El Paso and Hudspeth counties, which keep Mountain time). One date for every item.
